- Build fails on: any test failure, coverage below threshold, flaky test, perf regression, lint/typecheck/`cargo deny check` failure, or the door step above not reading either arm's sentence (the three-layer sentence or the bridge sentence).

`cargo xtask pre-push:linux` (2026-09-29) is the local Linux pre-push check — native on the Linux dev host since chunk 2026-10-09-pre-push-check-native-on-linux (Linux alone; any other system reads `cannot-evaluate` / `not-linux`; from 2026-10-03 until that chunk its six stages were run by hand under a founder ruling, the port carried from 0.3.0 and built as P-103); not a CI step: it reads its two pins from the repo (the Rust channel, ci.yml's Node major), probes the host (a missing piece is `cannot-evaluate` / `provisioning-missing`, named in `missing[]`, never green; it installs nothing), resets its per-run area `target/pre-push/run/` once provisioning has passed, and runs `script-modes` · `source-lint` (`cargo xtask check:english-sources`, since 2026-10-01 — the same English-only gate as ci.yml's lint-test step) · `npm` · `clippy` · `test` · `ci-gates` in the working tree, in order (six stages), each child under a cleared, constructed environment (no session bus, so the credential-store legs are expected to clean-skip in `test` — stated, not measured), first failure stops; the `test` stage's rewrite of the tracked bindings is put back as found. Since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed the sixth stage reads a real console engine cycle in place of a seed log it wrote itself: either cycle port (24317, 24318) already accepting is `cannot-evaluate` / `engine-port-taken` with nothing started; else `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle` runs on the stage data dir, the stage ends what it started (a port still accepting or the engine alive: `cleanup` once, and red), a cycle exit of 2 is `cannot-evaluate` / `engine-cycle-unevaluated`, and an exit of 0 hands the stage to `ci-gates` over the same data dir — eleven closed reasons. That the stage starts a program and binds two loopback ports is the operator's reading (the pc overseer, 2026-10-10), PROVISIONAL, the founder's own word owed; since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process that engine also opens the door's socket under the stage data dir, covered by the same item. Exit 0 green · 1 red · 2 cannot-evaluate, one JSON verdict of six members `{verdict, reason, head, tree, stages[], missing[]}` + `target/pre-push/report.json`. Its Node is the first `node` on the caller's PATH: on the dev host Node 24 is a user-level `mise` install beside the default Node 26, so the verb is started with that directory first on PATH. Measured green natively 2026-10-10 on `cb8cc4dc` (six stages, 89 s warm, 2836 tests, under load — a reading, not a budget), and with the sixth stage reading a real engine cycle four times at 107.04 to 110.44 s warm, the engine already built in release (the stage itself 18.8 to 19.0 s; no cold release build timed).

`cargo xtask perf:frame-sample` (2026-09-30) is the dev-host frame-budget gate — not in the standard gate set, not CI-wired (the hosted Windows runner exposed no WebGPU adapter): Windows only, it boots the release binary with a SwiftShader WebGPU flag set on the app child only, feeds `inject_demo --sustained` for 30 s, and grades frame p99 ≤ 33 ms with the frame arm required; exit 0 PASS · 1 FAIL (0 samples once healthy, or over budget) · 2 INCONCLUSIVE; opens a window. `cargo xtask perf:budget --data-dir <DIR> --require <arm,arm>` is its CI sibling — exit 0 PASS · 1 FAIL · 2 cannot-evaluate.

Not every harness command is a gate. There are now FOUR scenario legs, all deliberately outside the unconditional standard gate set and all dev-host-only (the third, `cargo xtask smoke:hue-shift`, grades the P-025 hue-shift samples by anchor; the fourth, `cargo xtask smoke:discovery` (2026-09-30), grades the P-027 discovery bound on a fresh boot — the first `metric.constellation.discovery_ms` within 5000 ms of the first `duckdb.append {table_name: spans}`, its own anchor within 1000 ms of that append, 0 panic and 0 ERROR; INCONCLUSIVE when no spans were appended, the webview was not polling first, or the data dir was not fresh; a window below 21 s is refused). `cargo xtask smoke:external-resolve` (2026-08-29) refuses at its precondition — the `andromeda-pulse-mcp` binary it resolves through is built by no target, its leg against the console engine owned by the route entry «Scenario legs driven against the console engine» (CARRY 2); its form drives the app-registry-vs-durable-store divergence: boot → finite storm → resolve an incident through a REAL `andromeda-pulse-mcp` subprocess → observe two 60 s persist cycles. Its verdict keys on `reconciled_count` (≥ 1) and `declined_count` (0) and deliberately **NOT** on `item_count` — measured non-discriminating, since a mutation removing reconciliation still showed 2 → 0 in both arms (the finite storm auto-resolves inside the window). `--sustained` cannot drive it (constant error rate never trips the cue gate) and the injector must be backgrounded, or the 120 s auto-resolve window closes before the external write lands. Like its sibling it proves its own preconditions (INCONCLUSIVE, never PASS) and refuses an observe window below two persist cycles. `cargo xtask smoke:gap-resume` (2026-08-28) has THREE arms: `--sustained` (arm B) is gate-grade; **arm A became gate-grade on 2026-08-28** when the defect it reproduced was closed by the `duckdb`/`libduckdb-sys` 1.10502 → 1.10505 bump — it now exits 0 under a TWO-HALF precondition (the silence storm formed AND ≥1 append REJECTED on replayed identities, via `StormEvidence.append_rejections`), because arm A drives the injector with `--replay` and a clean drain without rejections would prove the collision was absent rather than survived; and `--reconnect-only` (`conflicts_with = "sustained"`) reconnects with no idle gap, which established that the idle window is not the trigger. **A red on arm A is now a real regression, and the standing instruction survives the promotion: never weaken, remove, or `--expect-absent` it** — it is the only on-demand reproduction of this defect class. Each arm proves its OWN precondition and may not borrow another's (the gap arm needs a silence storm — absent ⇒ INCONCLUSIVE, not PASS; the control arm needs its absence; the stormless reconnect arm needs FEED evidence instead, ≥1 `duckdb.append`). The former known gap is CLOSED: `observe_window_supports_verdict()` refuses an `observe_minutes` window below the 450 s stall threshold the verdict reads, rather than reporting a structurally-impossible PASS.

**RED-leg evidence depends on the defect's SHAPE.** A REJECT-shaped defect (write refused, batch failed) emits the ERROR it is measuring, so the clean-log assertion must not be applied to it. A **BLOCK-shaped** defect emits nothing — nothing returns, so nothing reports — and a RED leg over it carries 0 ERROR and 0 panics, which makes that same assertion pass VACUOUSLY; there the evidence of record is absence-of-progress (frozen `rows_ingested`, consecutive zero-delta `buffer.tick`s, `buffer.consumer.stalled`). Decide the shape before choosing the evidence.

**Process-end witness form (test-plan §3).** A record that must survive the process ending is witnessed by re-exec
children (`pulse-app/tests/integration_exit_cause_record.rs`): each child inits the sink on its own TempDir, ends
through ONE class, and the parent reads the `agent-latest.jsonl*` family after the child ended — child-ran proof is the
child's own `app.boot.tracing.init` record (its stdout is discarded, so `--no-capture` shows nothing). A once-flag whose
sink's only drain is a guard drop is pinned by the emitter's RETURN value (the first flush closes the sink; a file read
passes with the flag removed). `cfg(unix)` arms run natively in `cargo nextest run --workspace` on the Linux dev host (2575 = 2573 + the two arms) and in CI `lint-test` on `ubuntu-22.04` (no macOS CI witness since chunk 2026-10-09-ci-on-linux-alone), not on Windows.
- NEVER `sleep(N)` for sync — wait for `health` polling or Channel events.
- NEVER mock OTLP receiver under test — use live `tonic`/`reqwest` to loopback.
- NEVER mock DuckDB at integration — use ephemeral `duckdb::open_in_memory()`.
- NEVER pre-populate test DB via `.sql` scripts — self-bootstrapping fixtures only.
- NEVER use `std::time::Instant::now()` / `chrono::Utc::now()` without injection — `tokio::time::pause()` for determinism.
- NEVER tolerate flake — quarantine and fix immediately.
- NEVER ship release with known test failures.
- NEVER include "human verifies canvas" steps — pixel inspection out of agent-driven scope.

- ~~NEVER allow OTLP self-dialing — negative test must assert prevention.~~ **DEPRECATED 2026-05-08** — by-construction-satisfied per obs-plan.md `2026-05-02 — Phase 3.5 pivot to tracing-only self-observation` (no OTel SDK in self-observation runtime → no exporter to misconfigure → no `ANDROMEDA_OBSERVER_URL`-shaped variable exists → trigger is unimplementable). The architectural "must-never-exist" guard for `ANDROMEDA_OBSERVER_URL` remains in `gotchas.md` §Self-observation. The test-plan body sites — the §1 entity row `Self-observation loop prevention`, the §1 trigger row `No self-OTLP dialing` and the §11 Project-specific bullet — now state it as `by-construction-satisfied` (no test generated, no negative test required); the deprecation history is in test-plan-amendments.md. Per amendments `2026-05-08T17-28-26Z-deprecate-self-otlp-loop-test` (Decisions Log only) + `2026-05-08T21-00-00-obs-pivot-test-bodies` (body annotations).
- NEVER dump raw OTLP JSON as snapshot — assertion requires dedup count + anomaly markers + p50/p95/p99 aggregates.
- NEVER skip post-`prost` invariant negative tests.
- NEVER assert receiver bound to `0.0.0.0` succeeds.

body: The following test triggers are documented but not yet implemented; they are deferred to the next `/andromeda-tests` re-run rather than processed via delta-rerun, because each requires dedicated harness design (xtask test command + fixture pattern) beyond cross-reference scope.
**PII vector test gaps** (security plan §Logging vectors 2/3/4/6 currently lack triggers; test plan covers vector 5 only):
- `security-vector-coverage: AppError sanitization` — assert IPC error response excludes stack traces / file paths / Rust struct names / library versions; grep on `agent-latest.jsonl` after IPC error
- `security-vector-coverage: Plugin path basename only` — load plugin with symlink chain → assert resolved path NOT in logs, only basename

- `security-vector-coverage: MCP response body redaction` — LANDED, no longer pending: `pulse-app/tests/security_mcp_response_body_redaction.rs` calls `query_traces` through the door of a spawned console engine over spans whose `service.name` carries a marker and asserts the marker 0 times in the engine's log family
- `security-vector-coverage: Path env var canonicalization log redaction` — set `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_PLUGIN_DIR=../../etc/passwd` → assert canonicalization rejects + logs only basename
- Per amendment `2026-05-08T17-28-27Z-document-pii-vector-test-gaps`.

**Capability widening static analysis — LANDED, gap closed** (security plan §API Anti-Patterns 3 NEVER-widen bans; `capability-drift` alone only checks TauRPC↔capability sync, which is why a second gate was needed):

- `security-vector-coverage: Capability widening static analysis` — shipped as `cargo xtask capability-widening-check` (chunk #77; CI-wired chunk #99; part of the §3 standard gate set since 2026-08-14). Parses each `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` and asserts: (a) `pulse:notification` contains only outbound emit permissions (no input handlers); (b) `pulse:tray` contains only outbound menu/icon permissions (no incoming-event handlers); (c) `pulse:plugin-fs` permissions limited to read of resolved plugin dir, no write/delete/execute, never exposed to webview JavaScript. Test fails with named permission and capability on widening detection.
- Per amendment `2026-05-08T17-28-29Z-document-capability-widening-test-gap`.

**Boot smoke check gap** (chunks touching boot/setup paths lack runtime smoke gating; chunk #27/#30 latent panic at `crates/ui-bridge/src/health.rs:291` went undetected through 4 wrap cycles before chunk #31's Phase 2b smoke gate caught it):

- `boot-smoke-coverage: per-chunk Tauri dev smoke gate` — chunks touching `pulse-app/src/main.rs`, `pulse-app/src/engine_boot.rs` (since chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point the process start `init_process` and the whole engine composition `start`, which both programs boot through, live there), `crates/ui-bridge/src/`, `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` (boot-time obs init), `pulse-app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, OR `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` MUST include `npx @tauri-apps/cli dev` (60s timeout; boot-completion signal detection: `Local:` / `ready in` / `Compiled successfully`) in their Test Commands. The direct-binary smoke variant (fresh `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` + env-gated mode + sustained `inject_demo`) is the accepted alternative where that form cannot express the needed runtime state — test-plan §3. On Phase 2b smoke failure, chunk surfaces "green per scope; runtime blocked" variant per /andromeda-implement Phase 3 — chunk implementation commits as-is; runtime blocker addressed via suggested redirect skill OR follow-up chunk. A chunk touching `pulse-app/src/console.rs` or `pulse-app/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-engine.rs` takes the spawned-program test `pulse-app/tests/integration_console_engine.rs` as its runtime gate; the window smoke boots `pulse-app` alone. Since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine `boot engine` (sh only) is the same direct-binary form over `target/release/andromeda-pulse-engine run`, and one whole run of the console engine under the harness is the Engine cycle gate form (`cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle`, test-plan §3).
- Per amendment `2026-05-09T16-00-54Z-smoke-check-boot-discipline`.

**Chunk-plan standard-gate baseline gap** (chunks #35-#36 committed with pre-existing fmt + tsc failures because their plan gate lists were incomplete; chunk #37's plan included the full set and exposed the inherited failures):

- `chunk-gate-baseline-coverage: standard gate set unconditional per chunk` — every `/andromeda-phase`-authored chunk plan's `## Test Commands` MUST list the FULL standard gate set: `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` + `cargo xtask capability-widening-check` + `cargo xtask check:ingest-progress` + `cargo xtask check:staged-artifacts` (staged git-index bindings + capability grants vs their pins; exit 0/1/2) + `cargo xtask capability-drift` (BEFORE the default-features workspace nextest, which rewrites `bindings/index.ts` in the default build's shape, the whole procedure set, so it does not shrink the bindings — overseer directive 2026-09-30; since 2026-08-30-staged-bindings-assertion the staged assertion is CODE folded into this gate itself) + `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` + the `emit_taurpc_bindings` regen, with no feature (the last cargo-adjacent step) + `git diff --quiet <chunk-base> -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` (the close, for a chunk adding no procedure; a chunk that CHANGES the procedure set closes instead with a content probe on the regenerated worktree bindings (the new procedure's name) → `git add` of the bindings WITH the `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` pin → `check:staged-artifacts`, then `capability-drift` LAST, and runs the regen BEFORE the `ui/dist` build and every release build a live leg drives — test-plan §3, measured 2026-09-30) + (when chunk's `Files-to-modify`/`New-files-to-create` lists touch any `pulse-app/ui/**` paths) `npm run lint --prefix pulse-app/ui` + `npm run typecheck --prefix pulse-app/ui` + `npm run test --prefix pulse-app/ui`. Webview gates excluded only when chunk touches zero `pulse-app/ui/**` paths. A plan that lists a build-branch push lists the merge-base probe directly before it, on the operator leg (`m="$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | cut -f1)" && test -n "$m" && git merge-base --is-ancestor "$m" HEAD`, `expect = ['exit 0']`): red when the build branch does not contain the remote's `main` as it stands then, brought to the operator before any push — the pull-request run builds the tip merged with `main`, the local pre-push check the tip alone (test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline, since 2026-10-10). Boot-smoke conditional per existing `boot-smoke-coverage` trigger (cumulative, not exclusive). Pre-flight gate parity at chunk-plan authoring time prevents the carry-over accumulation that delays detection by N chunks.
- Per amendment `2026-05-10T12-41-03Z-mandate-standard-chunk-gates`.

**The door's interrupt of a real query (NEW 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process).** `door-timeout-interrupt-real-query-coverage` — a door call over its 5 s bound answers `-32002` and the door interrupts its own read connection; the bound, the answer and the next call are pinned in process over a stand-in whose interrupt is only counted, and that the interrupt ends a REAL running query is shown at no tier. Owner: the route entry `Door admission lifecycle and bounds`.

**Living-artifact tooling re-run discipline — RETIRED 2026-08-26, its subject no longer exists.** `living-artifact-tooling-rerun-coverage` required wrap-session Phase 5 to run the Tooling command of each `.andromeda/context/{artifact}.md`; both artifacts (`api-surface.md`, `dependency-tree.md`) were deleted at commit `5a83771` (2026-06-28) and no `context/` directory exists. The code-graph (`.andromeda/cache/{plane}/tree.db`, derived, gitignored, rebuilt on demand) replaced them and has no LIVING block to reconcile. The row is kept in test-plan §1 for audit.
Full plan: `.andromeda/test-plan.md`.
- **`main`** — protected; all commits land via PR; never force-push.
- **Feature branches:** `feat/<short-name>`, `fix/<short-name>`, `chore/<short-name>` per task. Created from `main`, merged via squash+rebase PR.
- **Release branches:** `release/v<X.Y.Z>` only when needed for a release stabilization window; tagged from this branch.
- `feat: …` — new feature
- `fix: …` — bug fix
- `refactor: …` — code change without behavior change
- `chore: …` — tooling, deps, CI, formatting
- `docs: …` — documentation only
- `test: …` — test additions / changes
- `perf: …` — performance improvement
Scope optional: `feat(ingest): add OTAP wire format flag`.
Body wrapped at 72 cols; "why" not "what."
Co-Authored-By footer when AI-assisted: `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- Use `gh` CLI for ALL GitHub operations (do NOT suggest MCP or web UI).
- Title: short imperative (under 70 chars). Body has Summary + Test plan sections.
- One topic per PR — split if it touches multiple unrelated concerns.
- All CI gates must pass before merge: lint + clippy + nextest + coverage thresholds + supply-chain + a11y + capability-drift + staged-artifacts.
- Squash on merge (single conventional commit per PR).
1. Open release PR: `chore: prepare v<X.Y.Z>` — bumps `Cargo.toml` workspace version + updates `CHANGELOG.md`.
2. Merge to `main`.
3. Tag `v<X.Y.Z>` on `main`.
4. Push tag — triggers `release.yml` (tauri-action build matrix → Azure Key Vault EV signing → Apple Developer ID notarization → GitHub Releases upload).
5. `update-channels.yml` triggers on `release.yml` completion (Homebrew tap + Scoop manifest).
6. `production-release` GitHub Environment requires manual approval before signing secrets are accessed.
7. Verify auto-update flow on a test installation before announcing.

title: CI gates (PR cannot merge if any fails)

data.head: ## CI gates (PR cannot merge if any fails)

body: - `cargo fmt --check` clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` passes (zero failures, zero flakes — flake = real bug per Standard tier)
- Coverage ≥75% line / ≥85% function (`cargo llvm-cov`); a report that tracks nothing fails; the ≥70% branch threshold is retired as never measured, PROVISIONAL until the founder's word

- Performance budgets respected (snapshot p99 ≤500ms, memory max ≤512 MB, WebGPU frame p99 ≤33ms — graded by `cargo xtask perf:budget`, which CI runs on lint-test Linux with memory + snapshot required; the frame arm by `cargo xtask perf:frame-sample` on a Windows dev host (software WebGPU adapter), since hosted runners expose no WebGPU adapter; no bench suite exists, so nothing covers regression against an earlier run)
- `cargo audit` zero findings above warning
- `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` clean (catches `tonic` 0.14/0.13 duplicate)

- `xtask capability-drift` passes (TauRPC procedures match the `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` pin — worktree AND staged git-index copies; staged `capabilities/*.json` grants match `staged_gate::EXPECTED_GRANTS`; `cargo xtask check:staged-artifacts` is the direct verb)
- A11y suite passes (axe-core no critical/serious, Lighthouse a11y ≥90, no new violation tuple vs the baseline committed in the tree)

- Console engine cycle passes (`cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle`, the `boot` job's `Console engine cycle` step): its `cargo xtask check:engine-log` grades the console engine's own log — no gap over 45 000 ms between consecutive `ingest.tick` / `buffer.tick` / `connection.tick` records (fewer than two is cannot-evaluate, never PASS), a family holding records with `rows_ingested` above 0, memory max ≤ 512 000 000 B, no `app.panic.fatal`, exactly one `app.exit` and it is last. No CI step makes the heartbeat-gap check over the window app's log

- `cargo xtask ci-gates` passes over the `boot` job's app log family (`agent-latest.jsonl*`): zero-spans (the family holds at least one record) and zero-panic (no `app.panic.fatal` record at level ERROR); an absent family is cannot-evaluate (exit 2), never a pass

```bash
# 1. Branch from main
git checkout main && git pull && git checkout -b feat/my-task

# 2. Iterate
cargo tauri dev                                  # hot reload
cargo nextest run --filter-expr 'package(my-crate)'

# 3. Pre-commit checks (mirror CI)
cargo fmt
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci
cargo audit

# 4. Commit (conventional)
git add <files>
git commit -m "feat(ingest): …"

# 5. Pre-push check (Linux dev host, ci.yml's Node major first on PATH), the merge-base probe, then push + open PR
cargo xtask pre-push:linux                       # six stages, the sixth one console engine cycle on loopback 24317 / 24318; exit 0 green / 1 red / 2 cannot-evaluate
m="$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | cut -f1)" && test -n "$m" && git merge-base --is-ancestor "$m" HEAD   # red: bring it to the operator; never clear it by a fetch, merge or rebase
git push -u origin feat/my-task
gh pr create --fill
```
- `/clear` between unrelated tasks to reset context.
- `/compact preserve: branch=feat/x, status=mid-refactor, next=fix-foo` for long sessions.
- Delegate research / codebase exploration to subagents (Explore / general-purpose) to keep main context clean. Subagents cannot run Bash — only Read/Glob/Grep tasks.
- For complex tasks: use Plan mode first, then switch to implementation.
- At session end: update `.claude/session-handoff.md` (decisions made, files modified, current branch, remaining tasks, blockers, last failed command if any).
- At session start: ALWAYS read `.claude/session-handoff.md` if it exists.
- SessionStart hook auto-injects on resume/compact, but NOT on brand-new sessions — read manually at start of fresh `claude` invocation.
- If handoff contains "Last Failed Command" — propose an alternative approach BEFORE doing anything else; never retry the same command.
- `/wrap-session` curates session learnings + reconciles living artifacts (dependency-tree.md + api-surface.md) at session end.
- Plans in `.andromeda/` are the source of truth: arch + 6 specialist plans + route → CLAUDE.md ecosystem materialization via `/andromeda-setup-project`.
- Re-run `/andromeda-setup-project` after any plan regeneration to refresh `CLAUDE.md` + `.claude/rules/` + `.claude/docs/`.
- Per-chunk implementation: `/andromeda-phase` plans the chunk; phase loop runs `/implement` to execute.
- `/wrap-session` at session end → reconciles living artifacts + curates Tier 2/3 learnings.
- `/andromeda-help` for full Andromeda system docs.
- Never ask for manual browser console / network copy.
- If `chrome-devtools-mcp` is available, open the browser directly via Chrome DevTools MCP and read the console.
- For Tauri webview debugging in dev: `cargo tauri dev` opens DevTools automatically when `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1` is set on Linux; Cmd+Opt+I on macOS; F12 / Ctrl+Shift+I on Windows.

Path-scoped rules for the desktop-webview surface (React 19 + Tailwind CSS v4 + react-aria-components + WebGPU canvas). Loaded only when Claude is working with files matching the `paths:` frontmatter above.

**Authoritative source:** `.andromeda/a11y-plan.md` §3 (Harness Contract; keyed: `.andromeda/registries/a11y-plan-contracts.toml`, the Bootstrap phases key among them) + §11 (Anti-Patterns). Tier=Standard (WCAG 2.1 AA full ~50 SCs) + AAA escalation **SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions** (motion-sensitive trigger).
- Prefer native HTML (`<button>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<dialog>`, `<label>`, `<input>`, `<table>`) over `<div>` + ARIA roles.
- ARIA labels supplement semantic HTML; they do not replace it.
- NEVER `role="button"` on `<button>` (redundant), `role="presentation"` on a landmark (conflict), or `aria-hidden="true"` on a focusable element.
- Required landmark roles per surface — `<main>` + `<navigation>` minimum on full dashboard layouts; tray menu is OS-native (no ARIA).
- Every interactive element MUST be reachable via Tab / Shift+Tab.
- Focus order follows visual reading order (top-to-bottom, left-to-right).
- `tabindex > 0` is forbidden — use natural DOM order per `tabbable` 6.4.x ground-truth.
- Modals (settings, investigation) trap focus via `focus-trap-react` 12.x with `escapeDeactivates: true`; Esc closes; focus restores to the triggering element.
- Compact widget: Esc minimizes to tray; focus returns to tray icon on restoration.

- Separate Tauri windows (findings / report disclosure): focus restores CROSS-WINDOW via first-party Tauri events (`findings:dismissed` / `report:closed`), NOT `focus-trap-react` `returnFocusOnDeactivate` (which cannot cross windows) — findings-dismiss → the widget FindingsCounter badge; report-close → the findings window. A cross-document disclosure trigger uses `aria-haspopup="dialog"` WITHOUT `aria-controls` (a dangling cross-document id-ref fails axe `aria-valid-attr-value`).
- Tray menu: arrow keys navigate items; Return/Space selects; Esc closes (OS-native, manual SR pass required).
- Every `:focus-visible` element shows the `--border-focus` token outline (3–4 px outset, color `#4A90E2` Earth Blue).
- `outline: none` is forbidden unless paired with an alternative `:focus-visible` style.
- Focus ring contrast ≥3:1 against adjacent surface colors (non-text contrast).
- Text on Base (`#1A1D24`): Primary `#E8EEF7` ≈8.5:1 ✓, Secondary `#B4BCCB` ≈6.8:1 ✓, Tertiary `#7D8697` ≈4.2:1 (large text only), Muted `#56606E` ≈2.1:1 (decorative only).
- UI component boundaries / focus rings / icons: ≥3:1 against background.

- State colors (Success Feedback Cyan `#17B3A3`, Error Alert Burgundy `#C7556A`, Info Earth Blue `#4A90E2`) MUST be paired with text labels and/or iconography — never communicate state with color alone (SC 1.4.1).
- Verify per-token-pair via `axe-core` color-contrast rule + `colorjs.io` 0.6.x custom assertion reading design tokens via `window.getComputedStyle().getPropertyValue('--color-token-name')`.

title: Motion and reduced-motion (SC 2.3.3 AAA + SC 2.3.1 A)

data.head: ## Motion and reduced-motion (SC 2.3.3 AAA + SC 2.3.1 A)

body: - Every transition (chrome AND the data-driven severity signature) MUST respect `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.

- The severity signature degrades to a static glow (no pulsing rhythm); hue still updates per cumulative incident severity. **The rule attaches to whichever surface actually renders** — measured 2026-08-21, the Halo State Pulse WebGPU canvas has NO production render site on desktop-webview, so today that surface is the constellation DOT hue (`severityToHueFraction`); the glow layer is DEFERRED to the next version (operator ruling 2026-08-29; design-system §Brand Identity owns the status), and when it lands the rule attaches to it too.
- All `--duration-*` tokens (`--duration-fast` 150ms, `--duration-standard` 200ms, Investigation Capture Collapse 350ms) degrade to 0ms under reduced motion.
- Motion duration ≤5s OR provides pause/stop control (SC 2.2.2).
- NEVER flash content >3 times per second (SC 2.3.1 — risks seizures).
- Use `useReducedMotion` hook from `motion/react` 12.x in React; apply Tailwind v4 `motion-reduce:` variants to CSS transitions.
- Verify via Playwright `page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })` + Lighthouse 13.x prefers-reduced-motion audit.

title: Target size (SC 2.5.8 AA, SC 2.5.5 AAA conditional)

data.head: ## Target size (SC 2.5.8 AA, SC 2.5.5 AAA conditional)

body: - Pointer targets minimum 24×24 CSS px (SC 2.5.8 AA baseline) — apply `--target-input-min` token.
- Touch targets 44×44 (SC 2.5.5 AAA) only if a future scope adds touch mode.
- Verify via `axe-core` target-size rule with `runOnly: { type: 'tag', values: ['wcag22aa'] }`.
- Every form input has an associated `<label htmlFor="…">` (visible, not just placeholder).
- Error messages programmatically associated via `aria-describedby`; required fields marked with `aria-required="true"` AND visible indicator.
- Error messages identify the specific field AND describe how to fix it.
- Live region for dynamic content: `aria-live="polite"` (non-urgent toasts) or `aria-live="assertive"` (urgent / error focus shifts).
- `role="status"` for confirmations; `role="alert"` for errors.
- Avoid stacking simultaneous alerts — debounce or queue.
- Snapshot generation: Generate button gets `aria-busy="true"` during generation; completion announced via `aria-live="assertive"` in modal.

- The `` has no built-in ARIA — semantics are enforced via a wrapper: `
…
` (a named `
` takes the implicit `role="region"`; never write the role explicitly — `no-redundant-roles`). **SHIPPED** at `ConstellationCanvas.tsx:229` since 2026-08-23-a11y-verification. The name is a STABLE literal, never the live state summary: a landmark whose accessible name tracks its data churns the screen-reader rotor. The summary is the region's DESCRIPTION instead — a visually-hidden `

` wired via `aria-describedby`, aggregate-only (lifecycle counts + findings tally; no service name enters the accessible tree). `role="status"` on it is deliberately omitted (a ~1s poll plus the dashboard's existing live region would stack announcements).

- WebGPU fallback message ("WebGPU not supported in this context") rendered as `font-body` text in `color-text-tertiary` whenever the adapter request yields no usable device (`navigator.gpu` undefined, a null adapter, a rejected adapter request, a failed device request) — must be screen-reader accessible.

_Extended from P1–P7 to **P1–P12** at chunk #99 (a11y-plan §1 "Surface set extension"): **p8** findings dropdown · **p9** diagnostic report modal · **p10** diagnostics view · **p11** constellation semantics · **p12** export preview — then to **P1–P14**: **p13** empty states (2026-07-08) · **p14** Investigate result/error/progress states (2026-08-23). Each carries its own axe spec plus a `keyboard-focus/widget-and-modals.spec.ts` focus spec. The universal minimums (SC 2.1.1 / SC 2.4.3 / SC 4.1.2) and the §10 SLO coverage apply across all fourteen. **Standing rule:** every new route/modal adds one axe spec in the same chunk._

- **P1** Full dashboard Traces: `<main>`, the named canvas `region`, and a sortable native `<table>` all ship. **Row-level** keyboard traversal is the contract (roving `tabindex`: Up/Down/Home/End move row focus, Enter investigates the focused row, Esc exits to the toolbar; the in-row Investigate button is `tabIndex={-1}` so the row is the single tab stop). Cell-level 2-D traversal is deliberately NOT the contract for this read-only 4-column table. **Note the retired claim:** these were once recorded as "required but NOT SHIPPED" — measured false 2026-08-23-a11y-verification. The `table` role was never absent, and the region was checked against `TraceTable.tsx` when it lives on the sibling `ConstellationCanvas.tsx`. **Verify a claimed ABSENCE against the component that owns the surface.**
- **P2** Investigation modal: `<dialog aria-label="Investigation Snapshot">`, Generate button → `aria-busy=true`, slider for token budget, `<status aria-live="polite">` progress.
- **P3** MCP tools reach the engine through the door (socket and stdio relay): no UI surface — not-assertable and omitted; the settings-modal focus order is P7's.

- **P4** Live trace list: `<region aria-live="polite">` with incremental rows; live updates do NOT steal focus, and the re-poll preserves the focused row (roving `tabindex` state is clamped, never reset).

- **P5** Compact widget Esc → tray restore: `<button aria-label="Toggle dashboard">` (opens/hides the dashboard, widget stays; also Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P) / `<button aria-label="Minimize">` / `<button aria-label="Close to tray">` (the titlebar ✕ that hides the widget to the tray; Esc also triggers it). There is no `"Minimize to tray"` control — that accessible name has zero occurrences in the codebase (measured 2026-08-23).
- **P6** Snapshot completion: `<status aria-live="assertive">` final completion message + OS notification accessible via OS a11y API.
- **P7** Settings form: `<dialog aria-label="Settings">` / `<form>` / `<label>` per input / `<radiogroup>` / Tab cycle theme→position→retention→preset→Save→Cancel; Esc closes.
- `@axe-core/playwright` 4.11.x for E2E + `axe-core` 4.11.x standalone — `runOnly: { type: 'tag', values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'] }`.
- `lighthouse` 13.x CLI — built-in a11y category + focus-visible + prefers-reduced-motion audits.
- `pa11y` 10.x / `pa11y-ci` 4.x with `--runner axe` for parallel rule matrix.
- `react-aria-components` 1.17.x (preferred) OR `@headlessui/react` 2.2.x — pick ONE; mixing causes style/behavior conflicts.
- `focus-trap-react` 12.x for modals; `tabbable` 6.4.x for focus order ground-truth.
- `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` 6.10.x — extend `'plugin:jsx-a11y/recommended'` (compile-time gate).
- `colorjs.io` 0.6.x for token-binding contrast assertions.
- `motion` 12.x for `useReducedMotion` hook.
- PR cannot merge if: axe-core reports critical/serious violation on desktop-webview; Lighthouse a11y score <90; keyboard focus order test fails; contrast verification detects token mismatch.

- Per-PR regression: the detector compares the run's `{surface, wcag_criterion, selector, severity, violation_type}` tuples with the baseline committed in the tree (`pulse-app/ui/tests-a11y/baselines/a11y-violations-summary.json`) — nothing is downloaded; fail PR on any new tuple, and on an absent baseline (exit 1 since 2026-10-10). Baseline re-established 2026-06-09 from a clean full-chain pass (chunk #99 v0.2.0 re-audit; 0 violation tuples) — the v0.2.0 regression baseline.
- Run via `npm run test:a11y` or `cargo xtask test:a11y` (reuses tests' E2E driver per binding contract).

title: Harness shape + per-surface spec discipline (chunk #99 re-audit)

data.head: ## Harness shape + per-surface spec discipline (chunk #99 re-audit)

body: - Axe spec files: `pulse-app/ui/tests-a11y/axe/p1–p14` (p8 findings dropdown / p9 diagnostic report modal / p10 diagnostics view / p11 constellation semantics / p12 export preview are the v0.2.0 extensions; p13 empty states 2026-07-08; p14 Investigate result/error/progress 2026-08-23) + `keyboard-focus/widget-and-modals.spec.ts`. Every NEW route/modal chunk adds an axe spec in the same chunk (p8–p14 are the template); fixture payloads live in `helpers/v02-fixtures.ts` OR inline in the spec when single-surface. `installTauriIpcMock` honours two response sentinels — `__mockReject` (settle rejected) and `__mockDelayMs` (settle late) — so error and in-flight states are auditable, not only settled-success. **Fixtures must be POPULATED:** an empty array renders nothing, so the sweep audits a blank region and passes by comparing nothing.

- IPC mocking: taurpc 0.7 invokes as `TauRPC__<router.path>` (NOT `plugin:taurpc|…`); the window label is read from `__TAURI_INTERNALS__.metadata.currentWebview.label`. Use `helpers/mock-tauri.ts::installTauriIpcMock` — hand-rolled mocks with the old shapes silently dead-end every route audit (the session-64 rot).

- Routing: TanStack Router uses BROWSER history — `/#/route` URLs never resolve. Specs/configs use real paths; static serving needs SPA fallback (`helpers/static-server.mjs`; pa11y runs through `pa11y/run-pa11y.mjs` for server lifecycle).

- Suite health: `npx playwright test --config=playwright-a11y.config.ts --list` verifies the suite still collects — NAME the config: the bare `npx playwright test --list` reads the deliberately inert default `playwright.config.ts` and prints 0 tests with exit 1 whatever the suite state (measured 2026-09-30) (the session-64 breakage was a list-time import failure that silently masked all route audits for 35 sessions).

title: Structured violation JSON (binding from obs §6 schema)

data.head: ## Structured violation JSON (binding from obs §6 schema)

body: Emit to `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/a11y-axe-core-results.jsonl` etc.; upload as CI artifact.
- NEVER use ARIA on non-semantic HTML (`role="button"` on `<div>` instead of `<button>`).
- NEVER overuse `aria-label` (visible `<label>` first).
- NEVER set `tabindex > 0` (creates non-natural focus order).
- NEVER hide important content from assistive tech (`aria-hidden="true"` on essential content).
- NEVER mix React Aria + Headless UI in the same app.
- NEVER claim WCAG conformance without machine-verifiable evidence.
_This section is owned by `/wrap-session`. setup-project preserves content added here on re-run._

- 2026-05-09: `<section aria-label="...">` automatically takes implicit `role="region"` per HTML AAM (Accessible Name and Description Computation); writing explicit `role="region"` on the same `<section>` is REDUNDANT and triggers `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` 6.10's `no-redundant-roles` rule with: "The element section has an implicit role of region. Defining this explicitly is redundant and should be avoided." The pattern was used pre-chunk-#31 across `pulse-app/ui/src/canvas/CanvasContainer.tsx` (chunk #28) + `pulse-app/ui/src/App.test.tsx` mocks (chunks #28-#30) but went undetected because chunks #28-#30 did NOT include `npm --prefix pulse-app/ui run lint` in their gate list. Chunk #31 added the lint gate and surfaced 4 instances (1 fixed inline in HaloCanvas.tsx + 2 fixed in App.test.tsx mocks + 1 fixed in CanvasContainer.tsx as in-scope-by-extension). Resolution: drop `role="region"` from `<section aria-label="...">`; testing-library `screen.getByRole("region", { name: "..." })` still finds the section via the implicit role. The implicit role is preserved iff `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`) is present — a bare `<section>` without accessible name does NOT take role="region" (it's a generic sectioning element). For the canonical canvas wrapper pattern: `<section aria-label="Telemetry traces chart"><canvas /></section>` (NOT `<section role="region" aria-label="Telemetry traces chart">`).

- 2026-05-09: For dialog-with-combobox patterns (Cmd+K command palette / autocomplete dropdown / modal search), put the `onKeyDown` handler on the `<input role="combobox">` itself, NOT on the wrapping `<div role="dialog">`. Two reasons: (a) `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` flags `role="dialog"` as non-interactive (`no-noninteractive-element-interactions` rule) — putting keydown on the dialog wrapper triggers a lint error on every fresh chunk; (b) the canonical WAI-ARIA APG combobox pattern keeps focus on the input throughout — Down/Up navigates the listbox via `aria-activedescendant`, not actual focus movement, so the input is the natural keydown source. Tab nav with `role="tablist"` is a sibling case: the tablist coordinates child tab focus but isn't focused itself; satisfy `interactive-supports-focus` by adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the tablist div (does NOT break roving — active tab still gets `tabindex="0"`, others `tabindex="-1"`). Both fixes verified at chunk #33 with `pulse-app/ui/src/dashboard/CommandPalette.tsx` + `pulse-app/ui/src/dashboard/TabNav.tsx` after a fresh-chunk lint gate caught the violations. Tests dispatching synthetic keydown events should target the same element (e.g., `screen.getByRole("combobox").dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent("keydown", { key: "ArrowDown", bubbles: true }))`) — events on outer wrappers won't bubble down to the handler.

- 2026-05-10: For backdrop click-outside dismissal on modal/dialog/popover overlays, do NOT put `onClick={handler}` on the non-interactive overlay `<div>` — `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` flags it via TWO rules in tandem: `click-events-have-key-events` ("Visible, non-interactive elements with click handlers must have at least one keyboard listener") + `no-static-element-interactions` ("Avoid non-native interactive elements ..."). Adding `role="presentation"` is contradictory (presentation removes implicit role; click handler reintroduces interactivity). The canonical resolution is to move click-outside detection to a `useEffect`-registered document-level `mousedown` listener that checks whether the click target is contained in a ref to the dialog content element: `useEffect(() => { if (!open || !clickOutsideEnabled) return undefined; const handler = (e: globalThis.MouseEvent) => { if (dialogRef.current && !dialogRef.current.contains(e.target as Node)) onClose(); }; document.addEventListener('mousedown', handler); return () => document.removeEventListener('mousedown', handler); }, [open, clickOutsideEnabled, onClose]);`. Esc dismissal stays wired through `focus-trap-react`'s `escapeDeactivates: true` + `onDeactivate` (which can call both `triggerRef.current?.focus()` AND `onClose()`). Pattern verified at chunk #37 (Modal primitive) — initial implementation used `onClick` on the overlay backdrop with an `event.target === event.currentTarget` check, lint flagged 2 errors at line 82, refactor to useEffect document mousedown resolved both rules cleanly. Trade-off vs the `onClick` approach: useEffect requires a ref on the dialog content + careful dependency array including `open` so the listener only attaches when the modal is actually open (prevents the trigger-click that opens the modal from firing the dismiss handler immediately). Production behavior unchanged. Note: `focus-trap-react`'s own `clickOutsideDeactivates: true` option is NOT a substitute when FocusTrap wraps the entire overlay subtree (clicks INSIDE the trap container — including on the backdrop — are NOT considered "outside"); separate document listener is required.

- 2026-07-07: MAKING A FETCH-ONCE LIST LIVE INCURS THE SC 4.1.3 ANNOUNCE OBLIGATION — when a chunk turns a static (fetch-once) webview data list into a live-refreshing one (adds a re-poll per frontend.md 2026-07-06/07), it ACTUALIZES the a11y-plan §1 P4 "Live trace list" surface, so SC 4.1.3 now applies: announce the empty→populated transition ONCE, POLITELY, via the EXISTING `StatusLiveRegion`/`useStatusAnnouncer` (never a new live element, never `assertive`, never per-tick). Recipe: a `useRef(prevRowCount)` + a `useEffect` on `rows.length` firing `announce(...)` ONLY on the `0 → >0` edge, then updating the ref (guards per-tick re-announce AND a mounted-already-populated false-announce). Focus is preserved BY CONSTRUCTION (SC 2.1.1 / 2.4.3) iff the re-poll updates the rows PROP and the list is NOT remounted — no `key` on the component, no subtree unmount — so the derived (`useMemo`) view re-runs in place, keeping component-local filter/sort (`aria-pressed` / `aria-sort`) and `document.activeElement`. So the frontend "add a re-poll" action carries a PAIRED a11y obligation: the polite once-announce + do-not-remount. Verified at 2026-07-07-traces-table-auto-refresh (`TraceTable.tsx` one-shot announce): the `p4-live-trace-list` axe spec stayed green (0 new baseline tuple); vitest asserts announce-once + focus-preserved + filter/sort-survive across a rows update.

- 2026-08-26: ESLINT'S `--rule` CLI FLAG CANNOT CARRY A PLUGIN-SCOPED RULE UNDER FLAT CONFIG — and fixing the shell quoting first HIDES this, because it converts one failure into another. `eslint . --rule jsx-a11y/alt-text:error` builds a TOP-LEVEL config object, while the plugin is declared only inside the `files: ["**/*.{ts,tsx,jsx}"]` block, so the run dies with `A configuration object specifies rule "jsx-a11y/alt-text", but could not find plugin "jsx-a11y"` (exit 2) even once the args are quote-safe. The lint:a11y script had BOTH defects: single-quoted `--rule 'x: error'` args that Windows npm/cmd passed through literally (failing with `No files matching the pattern "error'"`), and behind it this structural one. The fix is to pin the rules in `eslint.config.mjs` inside the same scoped block that declares the plugin, leaving the script a plain `eslint .`. Two things to check before assuming such a script restores lost coverage: the rules may ALREADY be at `error` in the spread `recommended` set (all five were here, so plain `npm run lint` had been enforcing them the whole time the a11y script was broken — no coverage was ever lost, the script just could not run), and a repaired lint gate must be PROVEN to execute rather than merely exit 0 — feed it a deliberate violation (an `` with no `alt`) and require the failure, per the chunk-#99 green-harness-that-never-ran precedent.

**Authoritative source:** `.andromeda/design-system.md` §Color Palette + §Typography + §Spacing + §Motion + §Anti-Patterns + §Self-Validation Protocol. Brand: NASA Deep Space Mission Control Station (Modern Artemis Design). Signature element: Halo State Pulse (WebGPU shader-driven).
The palette is derived from the user-confirmed Color World; library-shortlist palettes are STRUCTURE only, NOT literal values.
**Core:**
- `--color-primary` `#4A90E2` — Earth Blue (actions, focus rings, active states, healthy state)
- `--color-secondary` `#2C3E7F` — Stellar Indigo (panel backgrounds, secondary nav)

- `--color-accent` `#C7556A` — Alert Burgundy (alerts, errors, anomaly indicators); lifted from #8B2E3B per design-system-amendments.md 2026-05-03 (a11y SC 1.4.11 non-text 3:1 minimum). Now classified as non-text token (border / icon / large-text emphasis); body-size error text should use `--color-text-primary` paired with `--color-accent` border + icon per a11y "never color alone" discipline.
**Surface scale (borders-only depth strategy):**
- `--color-base` `#1A1D24` — Deep Control Gray (page/app background)
- `--color-raised-1` `#262A33` — cards, panels (2-3% lighter)
- `--color-raised-2` `#2D3139` — dropdowns, popovers, tooltips
- `--color-raised-3` `#343A45` — modals, dialogs (max elevation)
- `--color-inset` `#0F1117` — input fields, code blocks, Halo canvas background
**Text hierarchy (on Base):**
- `--color-text-primary` `#E8EEF7` — Status White-Blue (~8.5:1)
- `--color-text-secondary` `#B4BCCB` (~6.8:1)
- `--color-text-tertiary` `#7D8697` (~4.2:1, large text only)
- `--color-text-muted` `#56606E` (~2.1:1, decorative only)
**Semantic / feedback:**
- `--color-feedback-success` `#17B3A3` — Feedback Cyan (ISS-cabin lighting)
**Border progression (Earth Blue at varying opacity):**
- Subtle `rgba(74, 144, 226, 0.1)` / Standard `0.3` / Emphasis `0.6` / Focus solid `#4A90E2`

NEVER deviate from these hex values without recording the deviation in the amendment changelog (`design-system-amendments.md`). NEVER use Tailwind default palette (purple/sky/zinc/etc.) as brand identity. The Halo State Pulse signature element is the ONLY exception that uses radial gradient + blur.

title: Typography (locked: JetBrains Mono + IBM Plex Sans)

data.head: ## Typography (locked: JetBrains Mono + IBM Plex Sans)

body: - `--font-display` / `--font-body` `'IBM Plex Sans', sans-serif` — UI, humanist sans = "human-readable summary"
- `--font-code` `'JetBrains Mono', monospace` — data rows, immutable telemetry fact
**Sizes / weights** (per design-system §Typography table): Display 32/600, Heading 20/600, Body 14/400, Label 12/500, Code 12/400 (tracking 0.5), Data 12/400 tabular-nums.
Both fonts bundled locally as WOFF2 (CSP-safe per `script-src 'self'`); no CDN. Source: `pulse-app/ui/public/fonts/`.
**BANNED font families** (NEVER use as primary): Inter, Roboto, Arial, Helvetica, Open Sans, Lato, system-ui default, Space Grotesk.
- `--spacing-micro` 2px / `--spacing-xs` 4px / `--spacing-sm` 8px / `--spacing-md` 16px / `--spacing-lg` 24px / `--spacing-xl` 32px
All values are multiples of 4 — high-DPI crisp rendering + Tailwind v4 alignment + dense Mission Control grid discipline.
- `--radius-sm` 4px (buttons/inputs) / `--radius-md` 6px (cards/panels) / `--radius-lg` 8px (modals) / `--radius-full` 9999px (badges/toggles)
NEVER use organic curves. Mixed strategy: most chrome at sm/md; only badges + toggles at full.
- `--duration-fast` 150ms / `--duration-standard` 200ms / `--easing-out` `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)`
- Investigation Capture Collapse 250–350ms (supporting moment, EXEMPT from 200ms hard limit per design §Motion)

- Halo State Pulse breathing period (DEFERRED to the next version — operator ruling 2026-08-29, the glow layer neither built in 0.3.0 nor deleted from the spec; the live surface is the constellation dot hue) 4–5 s quiet → ~2 s under active flow (≈0.2–0.5 Hz; data-driven via WebGPU shader, driven by activity state — supersedes the chunk #31-era 0.8–2.4 Hz `throughput_hz / 1000` band per design-system-amendments.md 2026-05-29); opacity + blur modulation ONLY, never scale (P-026); blur radius 4–16 px per cycle mapped from cumulative incident severity; LCH hue interpolation Earth Blue ↔ Alert Burgundy by cumulative incident severity; connection state is an orthogonal grayout/desaturation axis; EXEMPT from chrome budget (separate WebGPU canvas layer)
**Hard limits (NEVER do):** parallax / scroll animations / spring physics / staggered reveals / 3D transforms / canvas-WebGL except Halo / opacity fades >200ms.

**Reduced motion (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`):** all transitions become instant (200ms→0ms, 150ms→0ms) — app-wide, token-bound. The Halo degrade-to-static-glow rule (hue still updates per cumulative incident severity) is a deferred-layer requirement that ships WITH the layer; the shipping constellation dot hue has no pulsing rhythm to degrade.

- **Custom SVG glyphs** (registered as React components at `src/components/icons/`): `aperture`, `telescope`, `constellation-grid`, `star`, `circular-pulse` — astronomy/Observatory metaphor, monochrome `#E8EEF7` default.
- **Secondary fallback:** Lucide or Heroicons for generic controls only — NEVER as primary visual language.
- Sizes: 16px (tray, inline labels), 20px (buttons, list items), 24px (card titles, hero).
- **Cards:** `bg-raised-1` + 1px subtle border + `radius-md` + `padding space-md`. Hovered: emphasis border. NO shadows (borders-only depth).

- **Inputs:** `bg-inset` + 1px subtle border + `radius-sm` + `padding space-sm`. Focused: 1px solid `--color-primary` + 3px outset `box-shadow rgba(74, 144, 226, 0.2)`. Error: `--color-accent` border (rgba(199, 85, 106, 0.5)) + message text `--color-text-primary` below — the accent is carried as border/icon only, never the body-size error text color.
- **Buttons (primary):** `bg-primary` + `text-base` + `padding space-sm horizontal + space-xs vertical` + `radius-sm`. Hovered: `#5BA5F0` (Earth Blue +10% lightness), 150ms ease-out.
- **Tables:** transparent rows + 1px subtle border between rows; hover row `rgba(74, 144, 226, 0.1)` instant; cells `font-data` 12px tabular-nums + space-sm padding.
- **Halo State Pulse canvas container:** `bg-inset` + 1px subtle border + `radius-md` + `padding space-md`; `<canvas>` fills container.
`prefers-color-scheme: dark` is default; light mode + auto via Settings, persisted to `~/.andromeda-pulse/config.toml`.
`script-src 'self'` per security plan §API Security CSP — no eval, no remote, no CDN. WOFF2 fonts bundled locally. WGSL shaders first-party inline or module-imported.
- NEVER use generic font families as primary (banned list above).
- NEVER use Tailwind default palette colors as brand identity.
- NEVER use gradient overlays / glassmorphic effects on dashboard chrome (Halo State Pulse is the ONLY exception).
- NEVER use the same layout for different information types — metric display ≠ form ≠ data table ≠ status page.
- NEVER use color purely for decoration — every color encodes meaning per the palette.
- NEVER converge on safe defaults (sidebar + card grid, hero→features, form-in-card) — interface emerges from Observatory / Mission Control domain.
- NEVER use uniform monochrome status icons (green ✓ / red ✗) — Halo encodes activity-driven breathing rhythm + cumulative-incident-severity hue independently.
- NEVER use bounce easing or animations >250ms in chrome (supporting moments at 350ms exempt per design §Motion).
- NEVER use generic stock icons across chrome — custom Observatory glyphs first.
**desktop-webview specific bans:**
- NEVER ship visible Chromium/WebView2 artifacts (default context menu, dev tools, text selection on non-text).
- NEVER use unstyled web scrollbars (apply Tailwind v4 `scrollbar-*` utilities, dark bg + Earth Blue thumb).
- NEVER use browser navigation chrome (back/forward, URL bar).
- NEVER use hover-only interactions without keyboard alternatives.
- NEVER make windows non-resizable without strong justification.
- NEVER use `alert()` / `confirm()` / `prompt()` — use the first-party `Modal` on `react-aria-components`.
1. **Swap test** — replace fonts/palette/icons/Halo with Inter + Tailwind defaults + Lucide + spinner; if no meaningful difference → defaulted, redo.
2. **Squint test** — blur eyes; hierarchy still perceptible? Nothing screams?

3. **Signature test** — is the severity signature present on the surfaces that actually render? Path-scoped rules for the desktop-webview React frontend (Tauri 2 webview).

**Authoritative source:** `.andromeda/design-system.md` §Surface desktop-webview + `.andromeda/layout-templates.md` desktop-webview surface + `.andromeda/architecture.md` §Cross-cutting Patterns Webview IPC capability policy.
- **Framework:** React 19.x (Vite + TanStack Router)
- **CSS:** Tailwind CSS v4.x with `@theme` block (consumes `--color-*` / `--spacing-*` / `--font-*` / `--duration-*` tokens)

- **Component library:** `react-aria-components` + Tailwind (the SHIPPED stack — corrected as measured 2026-08-30: shadcn/Radix never landed; radix is lockfile-absent and denylisted by `pulse-app/ui/npm-policy.json`)
- **Canvas:** WebGPU `<canvas>` + `navigator.gpu` + WGSL shaders (the constellation canvas today; the deferred Halo State Pulse and Latency River when built)
- **Server state:** TanStack Query for cached IPC responses + automatic invalidation
- **Real-time push:** Tauri 2 IPC `Channel` API subscriptions (`pulse://stream/spans` etc.) decoded via `apache-arrow` JS package; updates flow into a Zustand store (NOT React state — VDOM diff cost)
- **Client state (local):** `useState` / `useReducer` for component-scoped
- **Client state (global):** Zustand for cross-component (telemetry stream cache, settings, panel layout)
- **Form state:** `react-hook-form` + Zod schemas matching the Rust `AppError::Validation { field, reason }` enum shape
- Frontend consumes ONLY TauRPC-generated `.d.ts` bindings — never manually re-declare command signatures.
- Generated bindings are the one tracked file `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` (all routers; regenerated by the test run — stage it together with any `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` edit).

- All backend errors deserialize as `AppError` discriminated union (`Validation` / `NotFound` / `Internal` / `Plugin` / `Storage` / `Ingest`); UI maps to user-facing messages without exposing `Internal { message }` raw.

- Real-time push: subscribe to `pulse://stream/spans` / `pulse://stream/metrics` / `pulse://stream/logs` through `streams.subscribe_spans` / `_metrics` / `_logs` (`Channel<Uint8Array>`; payloads are binary Arrow IPC); `pulse://stream/snapshot-progress` is the fourth contract event; `pulse://stream/plugin-events` is reserved but deferred — no runtime emitter.

- Adding a new TauRPC procedure REQUIRES its `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` pin in `xtask/src/main.rs` — `pulse-app/capabilities/` carries no per-procedure entries (one TauRPC invoke handler; measured 2026-08-21). The `xtask capability-drift` check enforces the pin in CI (and, since 2026-08-30, the STAGED git-index copies of the bindings + `capabilities/*.json` grants via the folded-in `check:staged-artifacts`). A new Tauri CORE API or `core:window:*` permission DOES need a capability grant, and is silently rejected without one — and a left-revoked or silently-added grant now reds the staged-grants assertion mechanically.
- The webview runs under `pulse:default` capability — webview cannot invoke `pulse:updater` / `pulse:plugin-fs` / Tauri core APIs (`fs`, `shell`, `dialog`, `http`).
- NEVER attempt to call Tauri core APIs from the webview without an explicit per-feature capability addition with stated rationale.
- Compact widget: no deep links (glance-only).
- Full dashboard: routable views per tab/sidebar entry — `/traces`, `/metrics`, `/logs`, `/snapshots`, `/settings`. Tab vs sidebar IA TBD downstream.
- Keyboard shortcuts (TBD): `Cmd+K` / `Ctrl+K` command palette or global search; `Cmd+Shift+P` / `Ctrl+Shift+P` widget ↔ dashboard toggle; `Esc` minimize widget or close modal.

- The canvas layer is SPECIFIED to sit OUTSIDE React's render tree — Arrow data pushed in via WebGPU compute shader, side-stepping VDOM diff cost. **Measured 2026-08-21: the Halo State Pulse canvas has NO production render site** (`<HaloCanvas` over `pulse-app/ui/src` non-test → zero hits; every reference is a `vi.mock` factory or a comment). The live severity signature is the constellation DOT hue (`severityToHueFraction` → `ConstellationDot.priorityTier`). The glow layer is DEFERRED to the next version (operator ruling 2026-08-29; the former build-or-retire fork is resolved — the render half rides `.andromeda/residuals.md`, target 0.4.0) — do not write code that assumes the canvas mounts.
- WebGPU init: `navigator.gpu.requestAdapter()` + device / pipeline / shader compile at component mount; reuse pipeline across re-renders.

- Fallback whenever the adapter request yields no usable device (`navigator.gpu` undefined, a null adapter, a rejected adapter request — caught since 2026-09-30 — or a failed device request; every `unavailable` result renders the shared fallback): `<canvas>` shows `font-body` text in `color-text-tertiary` ("WebGPU not supported in this browser"). MUST be screen-reader accessible (wrap in `<region role="region" aria-label="...">`).

- Frame timing emitted via TauRPC `telemetry.frontend.record_frame_ms(duration_ms, wgpu_backend)` for SLO enforcement (p99 ≤33ms per obs-plan §10 — the ms-form governs; ≈30 fps equivalence is descriptive only, per test-plan §12 2026-06-10 reconciliation).

- Reduced-motion: the Halo degrade to static glow (no pulse rhythm; hue still updates per cumulative incident severity) is a deferred-layer requirement that ships WITH the glow layer; the shipping constellation dot hue has no pulsing rhythm to degrade, and the token-level overrides carry the mandate. Use `useReducedMotion` hook from `motion/react` 12.x.
- `data-tauri-drag-region` on titlebar container (full width except buttons).
- Frame: `decorations: false` in `tauri.conf.json`.
- Window controls: traffic-light buttons left side on macOS (OS chrome convention); minimize/maximize/close right side on Windows/Linux at 32px from edge.
- High-DPI: React + browser handle `devicePixelRatio` automatically; no manual scaling logic.
- React 19 Compiler v1.0 auto-memoizes — do NOT manually wrap with `useMemo` / `useCallback` unless profiling shows necessity.
- Avoid React.memo unless a clear performance win is measured.
- Server components are NOT applicable (Tauri webview is fully client-side); avoid RSC patterns.
- Code-split at route boundaries via TanStack Router lazy loaders.
- Lazy-load below-the-fold panels (Snapshots view, Plugin manager).
- Real-time data updates: route through Zustand store, NOT React state (VDOM diff cost at 10k spans/sec is unacceptable).

- Frontend timing telemetry goes through the hand-rolled TauRPC `telemetry.frontend.record_*` bridge (frame timing, skeleton-pulse, the delegated timing observables) — `web-vitals` and `record_web_vital` were RETIRED 2026-08-30 (never installed; never a registered procedure): do not add the package or the procedure.
- NEVER fetch inside render — move to effect, IPC subscription, or loader.

- Always handle loading / error / empty states explicitly, error checked FIRST (skeleton component for loading; empty — the shared `EmptyState`: a `font-body` 14px message + the OTLP-port hint (`:4318` / `:4317`) in `--color-text-secondary` (#B4BCCB), never `--color-text-tertiary`, shown only after a settled zero-data load; error — a distinct `EmptyState` variant: a static "Couldn't load" message in `--color-text-secondary`, no exporter hint, never the raw `AppError`, with `--color-accent` only on an optional icon / border).
`script-src 'self'` (no eval, no remote, no CDN). WOFF2 fonts bundled locally. WGSL shaders first-party inline or module-imported.
See `.claude/rules/a11y.md` for full WCAG discipline. Quick reference:
- Semantic HTML first (`<button>`, `<dialog>`, `<table>`, `<label>`).
- All interactive elements keyboard-navigable (Tab/Shift+Tab/Enter/Space/Arrow/Esc).
- Focus ring: `--border-focus` token (`outline 3px solid #4A90E2`); never `outline: none` without alternative.
- Reduced-motion respect on every transition + Halo State Pulse.
See `.claude/rules/design-tokens.md` for full token spec + component patterns + Self-Validation Protocol. Quick reference:
- NASA Deep Space palette (Earth Blue / Alert Burgundy / Status White-Blue / Stellar Indigo / Feedback Cyan).
- IBM Plex Sans (UI) + JetBrains Mono (data) — bundled WOFF2 locally; banned: Inter, Roboto, Arial, Helvetica, Open Sans, Lato, system-ui, Space Grotesk.
- Borders-only depth strategy (no shadows on dark surfaces).
- Expression level 0.35: max 2 high-impact moments (Halo Pulse + Investigation Capture Collapse).
- NEVER ship visible Chromium/WebView2 artifacts (default context menu, dev tools open, text selection on non-text elements).
- NEVER use unstyled web scrollbars — apply Tailwind v4 `scrollbar-*` utilities (dark bg + Earth Blue thumb).
- NEVER use browser navigation chrome (back/forward, URL bar).
- NEVER use `alert()` / `confirm()` / `prompt()` — use the first-party `Modal` on `react-aria-components`.
- NEVER fight OS-level keyboard shortcuts (Cmd+Q, Ctrl+W, Alt+F4) — Tauri 2 respects by default.
- NEVER make the window non-resizable without strong justification.
- NEVER mix React Aria Components + Headless UI in the same app.

Shell mechanics of the Bash tool on this host: the recurring ways a recipe breaks. Every rule is measured on live
work, not hypothetical.

- The working directory MAY persist across calls (measured both ways on one host: persisted in one session,
  reset after every call in another) — rely on neither: anchor every cross-call path absolutely, or `cd` only
  inside a subshell `( cd X && … )` (setup's Bash guard denies a `cd` that would move the cwd); a
  `cd` inside a compound command can also trip a permission prompt.

- A zero-is-healthy count probe (`grep -c` / `grep -q`) exits non-zero on no matches and aborts a
  `&&` chain — suffix `|| true`, or chain with `;`.

- Never build JSON — or any multi-KB document — through shell quoting: `printf` collapses escapes
  content-dependently.

- Documents: the Write tool, whole-content (setup's Bash guard refuses a `cat`/`tee` heredoc with a file
  target). Ledger appends: a VALIDATED python append (`json.dumps(json.loads(...))` — a mangled payload fails
  loudly instead of landing).

- Inline `python -c` is fine for a SHORT, quote-free, single-expression probe; anything longer,
  quote-bearing, or document-carrying goes through a scratchpad file run by path (the measured failure
  modes are size and unquoted expansion, not inlining or quoted heredocs).

- `rm -rf` + `mkdir` + launch compounds get denied by permission layers and abort mid-chain —
  granular steps, fresh unique dirs, no `rm` in a launch path.
- `;` over `&&` for optional probes: an optional probe's failure must not abort the chain.

- Never `pgrep -f` / `pkill -f` on a pattern the invoking shell's own command line contains — it matches, and
  kills, that shell. Select by `ps -eo pid,comm,args` and act on the pid.

- Read `$?` from the BARE command — `| tail` / `| head` report the pipe's LAST command's exit
  (measured green-masking red gates). Redirect output to a file and inspect the file.
- When a tool prints its own verdict, the printed text outranks an unisolated `$?`.

- Heredoc terminators must be column-0 and whitespace-exact — a padded terminator silently
  swallows the rest of the script.

- The repo pins LF through `.gitattributes` (setup appends the lines): `git ls-files --eol` on a pipeline file
  reads `i/lf w/lf`. Never write CRLF into a pipeline file, and never fix a terminator reading with a
  terminator-agnostic script.

- 2026-10-05: On the Linux host the Bash tool's working directory persists across calls and the cwd guard blocks only a LEADING `cd`, so a `cd` inside a loop or a compound command silently moves the session cwd for every later call — use absolute paths or a `( cd DIR && … )` subshell there.

- 2026-10-10: This host's user git config sets `diff.mnemonicPrefix`, so a commit-to-work-tree `git diff` prints `c/` and `w/` header prefixes where a commit-to-commit diff prints `a/` and `b/`: a probe that parses diff headers pins `--src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/`, and the host's git config is never changed to make a probe pass.

Path-scoped rules for telemetry instrumentation across Rust crates + webview frontend bridges.

**Authoritative source:** `.andromeda/obs-plan.md` §3 (Observability Harness Contract) + §10 (SLO Invariants) + §11 (Anti-Patterns). Tier=Standard. **Architectural choice:** `tracing` ecosystem only — NO OTel SDK linked into the self-observation runtime (recursion-free by construction: the JSON file at `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` IS the agent surface).
- **Crates:** `tracing` 0.1 + `tracing-subscriber` 0.3 (JSON formatter + `EnvFilter`) + `tracing-appender` 0.2 (daily-rolling file sink, non-blocking writer) + `tracing-error` 0.2 (SpanTrace).
- **NO OTel SDK** in self-runtime. The product's external OTLP receivers (`tonic` + `axum` + `prost` + `opentelemetry-proto`) parse wire format only — they do not require an OTel SDK runtime.
- **NEVER** add `opentelemetry`, `opentelemetry_sdk`, or `opentelemetry-otlp` as a self-observation exporter. The recursion concern is resolved by construction.

- **Canonical self-observation surface:** `tracing-subscriber::fmt::Layer::json()` writing to `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl`. The security-plan body holds current truth only: its pre-pivot `opentelemetry-stdout` references left the body and live in `.andromeda/security-plan-amendments.md` (amendments `2026-05-08T17-28-25Z-reconcile-otel-stdout-references` and `2026-05-08T21-00-00-obs-pivot-security-bodies`).

- **Init order at boot, before HTTP/gRPC bind:** load env (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL` / `RUST_LOG` fallback) → build `tracing_subscriber::registry()` composing the non-blocking file appender + `EnvFilter` + `ErrorLayer` (no stderr layer) → install `std::panic::set_hook` calling `tracing::error!(target: "app.panic.fatal", ...)` → park the returned `WorkerGuard` (`hold_log_guard`) + install the at-exit hook (`install_exit_hook`) + on Unix the SIGTERM/SIGINT listener → (everything up to here is `engine_boot::init_process`, the process start both programs call once, which also records the start instant and writes the pid file; `engine_boot::start` then binds the receivers and spawns the engine tasks; the console program `andromeda-pulse-engine run` has no event loop and ends by SIGTERM/SIGINT through the listener) → the window app alone spawns Tauri through `run_return`, its code to `exit_after_event_loop` (record `app.exit` → drop the guard → `process::exit` with the same code). `WorkerGuard::drop` is the file sink's only drain — a plain `run` ends in tao's `process::exit` with the worker undrained (a record emitted just before it reached the file 0/20, measured on Windows).
- `service.name` = compile-time `"com.andromeda.pulse"` (Tauri bundle id).
- `service.version` = `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`.
- `deployment.environment` = `"production"` (hardcoded).
- Register once at subscriber init via `Layer::with_default_fields([service_name, service_version, deployment_environment])` — every JSON line carries identity without per-call boilerplate.
JSON-per-line via `tracing_subscriber::fmt::Layer::json()`:

Optional fields: `trace_id` / `span_id` (W3C traceparent strings), `duration_ms`, `plugin_path_basename`, `query_id`, `param_count`, `token_count_actual`, `token_budget_limit`, `body_size_bytes`, `webview_backend`, `tray_api`, `wgpu_backend`, `dedup_count`, `anomaly_markers`, `p50_ms`/`p95_ms`/`p99_ms`/`max_ms`, `error_rate_percent`, `value`.

- **Path:** `<data_dir>/logs/agent-latest.jsonl`, `<data_dir>` from `resolve_data_dir()` — `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` when set, else `%APPDATA%\andromeda-pulse\` (Windows), `~/Library/Application Support/com.andromeda.pulse/` (macOS), `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/andromeda-pulse/` else `~/.andromeda-pulse/` (Linux) — per arch §Filesystem locations.
- **Rotation:** daily via `tracing_appender::rolling::daily(log_dir, "agent-latest.jsonl")`.

- **Single sink (app):** the file `agent-latest.jsonl` (always JSON) — no stderr `tracing` layer and no TTY pretty-print (measured at chunk 2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp); the `app.panic.fatal` record is file-only, stderr carries only the chained prior panic hook's own output.

- **Door relay (`andromeda-pulse-engine door`; no stdio sidecar exists):** its stdout carries the door's JSON-RPC 2.0 answers — ANY accidental `println!` / `dbg!` / library stdout write corrupts them for the agent. The console program's `door` word (the stdio relay `pulse_app::door_bridge`, since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door; PROVISIONAL with the door's item) has no sink at all — no tokio runtime, neither boot function, no subscriber, no record, file or pid file: NEVER write to its stdout anything but the door's answer bytes, unchanged, or to its stderr anything but the one fixed line `andromeda-pulse-engine door: the door cannot be reached` on exit 1; its calls are recorded only by the engine it reaches (`door.call` / `door.refused`).

- Span naming: `{module}.{operation}` (e.g., `ingest.grpc.export.request`, `duckdb.append`, `snapshot.generate.request`, `plugin.invoke.request`). Avoid high-cardinality names (no per-trace-ID names).
- `#[tracing::instrument(skip(req), fields(rpc.system = "grpc", rpc.service, rpc.method, span_count, traceparent))]` on tonic gRPC handlers.
- `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(traceparent = %tp))]` on TauRPC routers.
- `#[tracing::instrument(skip(input, output))]` on `wasmtime::component::Instance::call` host wrappers.
- NEVER hold a `tracing::Span` guard across `.await` without `.in_current_span()` — span context bleeds into unrelated tokio tasks, breaking trace_id correlation and bloating memory.
- Manual `tower::Layer` (or `tower-http::TraceLayer` for plain `tracing` spans, NOT OTel-flavored) on the axum router.

- W3C `traceparent` header (HTTP) and gRPC `grpc-trace-bin` metadata extracted at receiver entry; attached as a regular `tracing` field (`fields(traceparent = %tp)`); downstream `tracing::Span::current()` inherits.
- IPC envelope (TauRPC command struct) carries optional `traceparent` field; receiver attaches to local span.
- Real-time push streams (`pulse://stream/spans` etc.) carry trace context in Arrow metadata column `_trace_context` for end-to-end correlation.
- `tokio::spawn` calls use `.in_current_span()` to propagate.
- NEVER log raw OTLP attribute values — use `attributes_count` + `service_name_tag` only. `#[instrument(skip(req))]` excludes the payload at the source.
- NEVER log full canonicalized plugin file paths — basename only (`plugin_path_basename: "my-plugin.wasm"`).

- NEVER log the corpus encryption key, the `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_CORPUS_PASSPHRASE` value, or any key derived from it — not as a value, a field, or a presence flag. The secret env-var naming convention is `*_SECRET` / `*_TOKEN` / `*_KEY` / `*_PASSPHRASE` → redacted. (b) PROGRESS — a consumer can keep ticking while draining nothing: measured 2026-08-26, `rows_ingested` froze for 16 minutes while all four ticks emitted normally with 0 ERROR, and every liveness check read healthy. `buffer.tick` therefore also carries `rows_ingested_delta` + `last_append_age_seconds`; a delta of 0 across consecutive ticks WHILE the ingest channel still holds queued work is a stalled consumer, announced once per transition on `buffer.consumer.stalled` (after 30 such ticks = 450s, sited above obs-plan §10's 420s sustained-drain cap) and asserted by `cargo xtask check:ingest-progress` — which reads NEUTRAL, exit 0, over a family with no `buffer.tick`; the reading that cannot be neutral is the `progress` arm of `cargo xtask check:engine-log` over a console engine's log. `rows_ingested` alone can never separate a stalled consumer from an idle producer — both leave it static; the channel's occupancy is the discriminator.

- **Heartbeat ticks vs TauRPC `health` command:** these are TWO DIFFERENT liveness mechanisms; both must remain. Ticks = asynchronous emission for retroactive analysis (was the subsystem alive during this window?); `health` IPC = synchronous probe for active liveness (runtime health checks; the HARNESS legs read the out-of-process `cargo xtask harness:status` verdict since chunk 2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep — the `status` verb directly, the boot poll through `cargo xtask harness:ready`, which holds that verdict plus both receivers reading `accepting` — a connection accepted on each OTLP port and, since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed, this run's own bound record for that port in the log family — since chunk 2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed — the `health` envelope itself is unchanged). Implementations MUST NOT replace tick emission with `health`-only state, MUST NOT treat absence of tick as failure of `health` (or vice versa). No shared state between the two paths required. Per amendment `2026-05-08T17-28-28Z-cross-ref-heartbeat-vs-health` (`.andromeda/runs/2026-05-08T17-28-28-spec-amendment-cross-ref-heartbeat-vs-health/amendment.md`).
