- 2026-08-15: THE EMIT SITE IS THE AUTHORITY — for what an allowlist leaf must contain, AND for what a target's silence means. Two failure modes, one root cause (extends the 2026-05-07 `for_target` resolver-order entry, which covers choosing the target KEY; this covers its FIELDS and its evidentiary weight). (a) **Enumerate a leaf's fields from the emit site, never from a backlog entry, plan list, or spec bullet.** Those lists are written from intent and go stale against the code; a leaf that names 2 of the 3 fields a site emits leaves the target PARTLY redacted, which every gate passes — the allowlist test only asserts what you told it to assert. Grep the `tracing::` macro call before writing the entry. (b) **A target's zero is evidence ONLY about the code that writes to that target.** Before reading an absent or zero-valued target as proof about a code path, confirm that path actually emits there: grep for the target constant's writers. A target with a single writer fed by one producer says nothing about a sibling producer that logs elsewhere — and the two can look identical in a log. Both cost real investigation time this chunk: a three-field emit site was about to get a two-field leaf, and a `triage.cue.emit == 0` reading had been carried forward as evidence about a storm path that never writes to it (the storm producer logs `triage.pattern.storm.*`).

- 2026-08-21: COMPLEMENT to the 2026-05-07 `AllowList::for_target()` resolver-order entry — that one gives the LOOKUP order; this gives the safe way to enumerate what is actually REGISTERED. NEVER derive the registered target-key set by grepping quoted dotted strings: `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` carries test-module literals that are NOT registrations (`target: "buffer.tick"` at `:2738`, and a loop over `["ingest.tick", "buffer.tick", …]` at `:2786`), so a string grep reports keys that do not exist and any redaction conclusion drawn from it can invert. Enumerate from the registration call's first argument ONLY — `by_target.insert("…"` — then resolve each target through the full fallback chain (exact → strip `.tick` → first `.`-segment → `::`-prefix). Measured 2026-08-21: the string-grep basis produced a wrong "the fingerprint-feed trio is shadowed by an exact `buffer.tick` key" conclusion; the registration basis reversed it — no exact key exists, so `buffer.tick` resolves via the `.tick` strip to the `"buffer"` set at `:176`, which DOES contain `span_events_seen`/`fingerprints_computed`/`observer_invocations` (emitted under those exact names at `pulse-app/src/heartbeat.rs:210-212`). Same test-literal-pollution root cause as the CLAUDE.md 2026-05-30 producer-existence entry (`grep -v cfg(test)`), applied to a registry rather than a call graph. **[extended 2026-08-26 — the prescribed form above is itself insufficient, and fails SILENTLY.]** `by_target.insert("…"` as a single-line grep matches almost nothing here: most registrations wrap, putting the key on the line AFTER the call (`by_target.insert(\n    "metric",`). So the single-line form reports a registered key as ABSENT — the same inverting failure this entry was written to prevent, now via layout rather than test literals. Use a two-line window: `grep -A1 'by_target.insert(' <file> | grep -F '"{key}",'`. Measured at `2026-08-26-cadence-runaway-blocking-pool`, where BOTH wrong bases fired in one session against the same question: a raw string grep reported `interpretation.model.load` registered (it is — but the grep could not have distinguished a test literal), and the single-line form then reported the bare `metric` and `interpretation` keys ABSENT when both exist (`:1078`, `:1934`) [extended 2026-10-10: those two numbers are lines of `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` as it stood on 2026-08-26, the day of the measurement, not of any file as it stands now]. Two false answers were one step from entering a spec master as measured fact. **The discipline generalizes past this registry: when an entry prescribes a grep as the authoritative basis, the grep's own shape is part of the claim — verify it returns a known-present control before trusting a negative.** Here `buffer` (known to exist) was the control that exposed it.

- 2026-08-26: THE ALLOWLIST FALLBACK HAS A THIRD SHAPE — it can resolve to a POPULATED SIBLING set, which is worse than resolving to nothing. The two shapes already recorded above are (a) no bare prefix key exists, so `for_target` resolves NOTHING and every field redacts (the `app.`-prefixed leaves), and (b) a bare key exists carrying only `value`/`unit`/`module`, so a `metric.*` target keeps `value` and silently loses its labels. The third: a bare key exists AND carries a full, unrelated field set. `buffer.consumer.stalled` falls back to the `buffer` key — which holds the ten `buffer.tick` counters and NONE of that target's four fields — so the target RESOLVES SUCCESSFULLY and every field still vanishes. That is the most deceptive of the three, because a resolver probe asserting `for_target(target).is_some()` passes. Two consequences for any new dotted target under an existing module key: assert the leaf's field SET, never merely that it resolves; and pin a DISCRIMINATOR that the fallback set does NOT contain the target's fields — without it, deleting the exact leaf leaves the guard passing vacuously, which is exactly the failure the guard exists to catch. Verified at `2026-08-26-ingest-consumer-stall-under-sustained-load`: `stall_fields_are_absent_from_the_buffer_fallback_set` is that pin, and the leaf's own test asserts set equality in both directions (a narrowed leaf and a widened one both fail). **[extended 2026-08-26] A FOURTH shape needs no fallback at all: the target has its OWN exact leaf, and the leaf is INCOMPLETE.** Then `for_target` resolves to the right entry, the fields it names render fine, and only the omitted ones read `"<redacted>"` — a PARTLY redacted target that no resolver probe and no gate can see, because half the record looks healthy. It is how a target sits mis-diagnosed for months: the 2026-08-15 muted-diagnostic census recorded five targets as "resolving to no allowlist entry" when measurement found that true for exactly ONE — two fell back to the bare `metric` key, and TWO (`triage.cue.tick`, `interpretation.model.load`) had exact leaves missing a field each. **The mechanism decides the repair** — "complete the leaf" versus "add a leaf" — so a census that records the wrong one sends its owner to the wrong edit. Consequence for the guard: the set-equality assertion above is what catches this; a resolver probe cannot. Mutation-proven at `2026-08-26-cadence-runaway-blocking-pool` — narrowing `triage.cue.tick` back to its pre-fix 5-of-7 leaf turned the field-set and un-mute pins RED while `cue_tick_resolves_to_an_exact_leaf` **stayed green**.
Universal security requirements. Apply to all files in this project. This rule file has no `paths:` frontmatter — it loads unconditionally.

**Authoritative source:** `.andromeda/security-plan.md` (tier=Minimal — local-first Tauri 2 desktop app plus, since chunk `2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point`, the console program `andromeda-pulse-engine` over the same engine boot; loopback-only OTLP, in-memory DuckDB). For full threat model, vector list, and bootstrap phasing, read the plan.
- OTLP receivers MUST bind to `127.0.0.1` only — `:4317` (tonic 0.14 gRPC) and `:4318` (axum 0.8 HTTP). Loopback is the de-facto authorization boundary; no auth model.
- NEVER bind to `0.0.0.0` or any non-loopback interface — invalidates the entire Minimal-tier risk model.

- OTLP HTTP `:4318` MUST have Host-header allowlist middleware (reject non-`{127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1]}:configured-port`); DNS rebinding lesson from Coder Agent CVE-2025-09-19 + MCP TypeScript SDK CVE-2025-66414.
- OTLP HTTP `:4318` MUST have CORS deny-by-default — no `CorsLayer::permissive()` / `allow_origin(Any)`; no browser context should ever post OTLP.

- OTLP `:4318` MUST set `axum::DefaultBodyLimit::max(8 * 1024 * 1024)`; OTLP `:4317` MUST set `.max_decoding_message_size(8 * 1024 * 1024)` per `*ServiceServer` builder. JFrog axum-core advisory + tonic 1 GB-default issue are the anchors.

- Post-`prost`-decode invariant checks REQUIRED on every OTLP payload — `span_id` is 8 bytes, `trace_id` is 16 bytes, attribute keys/values bounded. `prost` only validates wire format; semantic invariants are the `ingest` crate's job.

- DuckDB queries MUST use `Connection::prepare` + `?` placeholders + `Statement::execute([&param])` — NEVER `format!("SELECT … WHERE service_name = '{}'", user_input)`. 2026 DuckDB CVE cluster (Dagster GHSA-mjw2-v2hm-wj34, Vanna CVE-2024-5827, dagster-duckdb CVE-2026-41490).

Opt-in rather than data-dir-default because the GGUF and `llama-cli.exe` live outside the data dir BY DESIGN — a default would reject every configuration that has run L4. **Residual consequence, scoped:** on a host that leaves the root unset, an actor who can set these vars can still point the product at an arbitrary on-disk file — read as a model, or EXECUTED as the inference binary. Accepted under this tier's local-single-user trust boundary, and no longer silent: the unconfined posture emits one WARN per boot on `interpretation.model.allow_root`. **The primitive here — and now project-wide — is `std` both-sides-canonicalize on the `publish_workspace_key` precedent** (`strict-path` declined at the 2026-08-26 P4 review, then dropped from the graph at `2026-08-29-advisory-backlog`). The sibling argv-prompt residual is CLOSED: `validate_prompt_bounded` bounds the `-p` value before `Command` assembly. **Ratified carve-out — the corpus-key lock dir (chunk `2026-10-04-corpus-key-creation-is-race-free`; founder ratification 2026-10-04):** both product binaries (`pulse-app`, `andromeda-pulse-engine`) read the system `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (Linux) through `Corpus::open` to place the content-free lock file `andromeda-pulse-corpus-key-{h16}.lock`; trimmed, then when set it must be absolute, `canonicalize()` and be a directory, else lock-dir resolution FAILS CLOSED (`KeychainError::Unavailable`, never a temp-dir fallback); unset/blank ⇒ the canonicalized `std::env::temp_dir()`. Data-dir confinement is omitted by design (the lock is keyed on the one per-user credential entry, shared by processes with different data dirs) — with the `~/Downloads` export sink and the per-spawn L4 grammar temp file in `std::env::temp_dir()` (since chunk #84; the committed GBNF since chunk `2026-10-05-l4-runs-the-founder-s-pick-with-its-authors-settings`) it is one of the THREE product-written locations outside the data dir. The L4 argv's other operands are first-party (founder-ratified 2026-10-05): the `--grammar-file` temp path holding the committed `L4_OUTPUT_GBNF` (`grammar_for_schema` refuses any other schema) and the sampling constants `--temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 64 --min-p 0` — `-p` stays the one OTLP-derived operand. A harness-only second reader of that bound (chunk `2026-10-07-l4-probe-reproduces-the-canary-history-miss`; a Boundary widening the founder answered 2026-10-07): the dev probe's `--replay` (`pulse-app/examples/l4_decision_probe/replay.rs`, an example binary, never shipped) passes a captured product prompt, read from a run-time path outside the tree, unchanged as its `-p` operand through the same `validate_prompt_bounded` and its own file checks (regular files, at most 64 KiB, UTF-8, a capture directory inside the work tree and outside `target/` refused); nothing of a prompt is printed, stored or committed, and the product's argv is unchanged.
- TauRPC procedure args MUST go through `serde` deserialization on every `#[taurpc::procedure]` argument struct; `TryFrom<u16>` on every port; `serde`-friendly enums on every settings field.
- Plugin file paths MUST canonicalize + confine under the resolved plugin dir before `wasmtime` load. Pair with the path-env-var canonicalization above.

- The test port claim is test-only and stated as built, with no class reading made for it (chunk `2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data`): ONE home, `test_support::ports::claim_port` / `PortClaim` in the dev-only member `test-support` (no product target links it; pinned by the `xtask` test module `test_support_edges`); a number from 20000 to 31999 (24317 / 24318 left out) under an advisory lock on the empty file `target/test-ports/{number}`, never unlinked; the directory comes from the crate's compile-time manifest directory — no environment variable is read at run time and none is added. Test-written, never product-written or product-read; no new place on disk, port range or listening socket.

- Every TauRPC procedure MUST have its `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` pin in `xtask/src/main.rs` (what `capability-drift` diffs — against the worktree AND, since 2026-08-30-staged-bindings-assertion, the staged git-index bindings, with the staged `capabilities/*.json` grants asserted vs `staged_gate::EXPECTED_GRANTS`) plus a validated argument struct — NOT a per-procedure `pulse-app/capabilities/` entry, which does not exist in this project (TauRPC dispatches every method through one invoke handler; measured 2026-08-21). Tauri capabilities remain NEGATIVE-DEFAULT at the IPC-layer and per-CORE-API granularity: `fs` / `shell` / `dialog` / `http` and each `core:window:*` permission require an explicit grant with rationale, and ARE silently rejected at runtime when missing.

- Two enforcement pieces required for a NEW procedure: (1) router registration in the owning crate, AND (2) its `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` pin in `xtask/src/main.rs`. The `xtask capability-drift` check enforces the pair in CI — and since 2026-08-30-staged-bindings-assertion it ALSO asserts the STAGED (git-index) copies: bindings vs `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` + every `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` vs `staged_gate::EXPECTED_GRANTS` in both directions (`cargo xtask check:staged-artifacts` is the direct verb; exit 0 staged-clean / 1 staged-drift / 2 cannot-evaluate). (A capability JSON edit is the enforcement pair for a new CORE API / `core:window:*` grant, not for a procedure.)
- NEVER grant Tauri core APIs (`fs`, `shell`, `dialog`, `http`) to `pulse:default` without an explicit per-feature capability addition with stated rationale.
- NEVER expose `pulse:updater` to webview JavaScript — bound to `tauri-plugin-updater` flow only.
- `pulse:notification` and `pulse:tray` MUST be outbound-emit-only — input-event handlers (notification action callbacks, tray menu IPC re-entry) require a separately-named capability.
- `pulse:plugin-fs` MUST stay scoped to the host's read of the canonicalized plugin dir — never widened to webview / write / execute.

- **The grants are held mechanically, not by review and runtime rejection alone:** `xtask capability-drift` asserts the STAGED `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` against the in-code `staged_gate::EXPECTED_GRANTS` pin (`{identifier, windows, permissions}` × 6 files; set equality in BOTH directions — a REVOKED and an ADDED grant each red, an unpinned capability file red, a staged subject deletion red), so a left-revoked or silently added grant is caught in CI and Tauri's silent runtime rejection is no longer the sole enforcement (security-plan §API Security; §Security Anti-Patterns → API). The static check of the three NEVER-widen bans above (`pulse:notification` / `pulse:tray` / `pulse:plugin-fs`) is `cargo xtask capability-widening-check`, a per-PR CI step (test-plan §1 Pending coverage triggers, LANDED chunk #77).
- WASM Component Model guests receive ONLY host imports declared in their WIT — no syscalls, file, or socket access unless explicitly granted.

- `wasmtime::Config` MUST set `epoch_interruption(true)` for plugin call timeouts (2-3× faster than fuel). The canonical wasi-http header field-size bound is the `MAX_WASM_HTTP_FIELDS_SIZE_BYTES` const in `crates/plugins/src/engine.rs` (chunk #45 substrate; CVE-2026-27572 anchor); actual enforcement attaches via `wasmtime_wasi_http::WasiHttpCtxBuilder::max_field_size` (or equivalent) when wasi-http imports are introduced in subsequent chunks (#46+). Per security-plan §Input Validation and §API Security (the 2026-05-11 decision is in the externalized Security Decisions Log, `security-plan-amendments.md`) — `Config::max_wasm_http_fields_size` is NOT a method on `wasmtime::Config` in any wasmtime version; the bound lives at the wasi-http context, not the Config struct.
- Per-Store `wasmtime::ResourceLimiter` MUST cap memory (e.g., 64 MB), tables, instances.

- Cranelift backend on x86_64 MUST stay enabled — was the unaffected configuration for April 2026 Critical sandbox escapes (CVE-2026-34941, CVE-2026-35195). NEVER add a non-Cranelift wasmtime feature flag on x86_64 builds.
- NEVER use the `wasmtime::Linker` to expose host functions outside the WIT contract — bypasses capability scoping.
- NEVER trust plugin-returned Arrow IPC bytes without a size cap before re-emit on the Tauri Channel API.

- The nine MCP tools are served through the console engine's door alone — hand-rolled serde JSON-RPC 2.0 framing (`crates/mcp-server/src/jsonrpc.rs`), name-dispatch via `mcp_server::tools::call_tool`, whose one product caller is `door::EngineTools`.
- `call_tool` returns `ToolAnswer` and writes no log record; `tools/list` gives every tool a boolean `write`, true for `mark_incident_resolved` alone.

- Since chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process` the console engine's door serves the nine tools, and it alone (no `rmcp`: it is in no manifest and not in `Cargo.lock`); the door's own controls are the next section's. Since chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door` a stdio agent reaches those nine tools over stdin/stdout through `andromeda-pulse-engine door`, the door's own controls are what hold it — a way through the door, not a second way in: the engine has one way in besides telemetry, this door, reached over its socket or through the stdio relay.

title: The console engine's door (owner only — PROVISIONAL)

data.head: ## The console engine's door (owner only — PROVISIONAL)

body: _A boundary widening, one item: the endpoint, the owner check, the reach of the nine tools and of the one write, the write-switch variable and the workflow step that runs a client as a second account are the operator's answers (the pc overseer, 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-11), and since chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door` the same item also covers the console program's third word `door` (the stdio relay) and the step's second arm (the operator's answers, 2026-10-12); the founder's own word is owed and nothing of it is ratified (security-plan §Threat Model Summary → Attack surface, the door's vector)._

- The door is a Unix-domain stream socket at `{data dir}/run/door/sock` (mode 0600, inside `run/door/`, mode 0700), opened by `andromeda-pulse-engine run` alone; the window app seats none; no TCP port and no network listener is added. The path is canonicalized, refused when it leaves the data dir, and must be shorter than 108 bytes; a door that cannot bind leaves the engine running with no door. Since chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door` the console program's third word `door` is the stdio relay to a running engine's door (a boundary widening, PROVISIONAL with this item): it boots no engine (neither `engine_boot::init_process` nor `engine_boot::start`), resolves the data dir through `engine_boot::resolve_data_dir`, canonicalizes the data dir and `{data dir}/run/door/sock` both sides and treats a socket that does not resolve, resolves outside the data dir or has a path of 108 bytes or more as unreachable; it reads standard input by line bounded at `door::MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` + 1 (an over-bound line's rest discarded, never sent), parses no request and sends each line on a connection of its own, the door applying every bound and the account check; an unreachable door or a failed socket or standard-output operation is exit 1 with one fixed standard-error line and nothing on standard output; it adds no env var, flag, value, listener, port, file, pid file or log record.
- NEVER write a byte to a door peer before its account is read from the kernel and found equal to the engine's own effective account (`door::admits`).
- NEVER admit root, or a peer whose account cannot be read.

- NEVER widen `run/door/` beyond 0700 or `run/door/sock` beyond 0600 — and NEVER treat those modes as the control against root: they do not hold it (measured on `ci#38097928056`); the account check does.

- Every request is bounded: one JSON-RPC 2.0 line of at most 65 536 bytes; the closed methods `initialize` · `tools/list` · `tools/call` · `ping`; the closed nine-tool set; `arguments` with declared members only (`-32602` before any tool runs); an answer of at most 1 048 576 bytes, never cut (`-32003`); a call of at most 5 s (`-32002`); 30 s idle; 8 connections; one tool call at a time. Every refusal carries a fixed message, never the tool's own error text.

- `mark_incident_resolved` is the one write: refused with `-32001` before the dispatcher unless `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DOOR_RESOLVE` is on (unset or `on` ⇒ on; `off` ⇒ off; anything else ⇒ off and `rejected`, fail closed, the value never logged).
- The door opens no database and no corpus, reads no `run/workspace-key` and prepares no SQL — it uses the engine's own handles.

- The tool manifest declares `additionalProperties: false` on every tool; the door's `declared_only` is the one refusal of an undeclared argument member — `-32602` for all nine tools before any tool runs, nothing of it answered (the argument structs carry no `deny_unknown_fields`).

- Every `#[taurpc::procedure]` returns `Result<T, AppError>` — `AppError` is the `serde`-friendly enum (`Validation { field, reason }` / `NotFound { resource }` / `Internal { message }` / `Plugin { plugin_id, message }` / `Storage { message }` / `Ingest { message }`).
- Module-internal `thiserror` 2.x enums convert at the bridge via `From` impls. NEVER serialize `anyhow::Error` directly across the bridge.
- `AppError::Internal { message }` carries a sanitized one-liner — strip stack traces, file paths, library versions, Rust struct names. Full chain stays in internal log via `tracing-error` SpanTrace.
- OTLP receiver errors collapse to standard `tonic::Status` codes / `Status` proto in body per OTLP HTTP spec.
- MCP server errors use standard JSON-RPC 2.0 error object (numeric `code`, `message`, optional `data`).

- NEVER log raw OTLP attribute values, span/log/metric content payloads, snapshot file contents, clipboard contents, or MCP tool response bodies — incidentally captured secrets from instrumented host apps. The `snapshot.generate`/`snapshot.copy_to_clipboard` resolver arm of this ban is UNVERIFIED (its only canary was dead-by-construction and was deleted at chunk 2026-08-30-dead-lib-src-test-migration — a test binary linking the resolver aborts at load; owed via test-plan §1 `snapshot-resolver-level-coverage`); the webview copy route IS wire-measured.

- NEVER log a full product-consumed filesystem path — basename of the canonicalized path only. Covers the plugin dir, the three L4 model/binary path vars, the `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_ALLOW_ROOT` root, the corpus-key lock dir / lock file (its failures surface only as the unit `KeychainError` variants → `KeyringUnavailable`, no path, no OS error text), and the per-spawn L4 grammar temp file `andromeda-pulse-llama-grammar-{pid}-{nanos}.gbnf` (never logged at all; 0× in the 2026-10-05 GREEN real-model leg) (`path_basename` / `root_basename` plus the env-var NAME, which is safe — only `*_SECRET` / `*_TOKEN` / `*_KEY` / `*_PASSPHRASE` names redact). Measured at the wire 2026-08-26: the model path's containing directory 0× across 11,251 lines, basename 1×, full root 0×. The rule is CATEGORICAL since chunk 2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep — the two boot records that carried a standing exception (`app.boot.tracing.init`, `app.boot.pid`) now emit basenames via `pulse_app::observability::log_basename` (boot smoke: 0 full paths).

- `app.boot.door`, `door.call` and `door.refused` (chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process`) are deliberate NO-SCRUB log boundaries, each behind its OWN exact allowlist leaf with no bare `door` and no bare `app` key: `{state, resolve_write}` · `{method, tool, outcome, write, result_type, result_count, answer_bytes, duration_ms}` · `{reason, peer}`, every field a closed label, a bool or a number. NEVER put on a door record an argument, an answer, a path (the socket's included), the peer's account id or an error's text; none is written at ERROR. `door.call` is written BEFORE the answer line. Stated limit: a tool called through the door also writes the tools' own library records into the console engine's log, not enumerated from a log.
- NEVER log DuckDB query parameter values — use `query_id` + `param_count` + `param_types` instead.
- NEVER expose internal hostnames / IPs / library versions in OTLP error responses or MCP error objects.
- `snapshot.copy_to_clipboard` MUST emit a `pulse://stream/snapshot-progress` event at clipboard-write time so the UI can show a non-suppressible "X bytes copied" toast.

- `ui.ipc.rejection` (chunk 2026-08-30-acl-rejection-logging) is a deliberate NO-SCRUB log boundary — the §Logging & Monitoring "capability-rejected IPC" record: a WARN once per rejection behind its own exact allowlist leaf, carrying ONLY the bounded triple `{error_category (closed enum acl_rejected|other), window_label (coerced 4+unknown), payload_bytes (u32, bounded)}`; the copied markdown, the command string and the raw rejection text are excluded by construction (wire-measured 0× across the revoked-run log). The clipboard NEVER-log ban covers EVERY clipboard-payload path, including this webview copy-failure route — never just `snapshot.copy_to_clipboard`.

- `ui.webgpu.adapter` (chunk 2026-09-30-perf-instruments-measure-their-budgets; a Boundary widening the founder ratified at P4 2026-09-30, «Да, делай») is a second deliberate NO-SCRUB webview-originated log boundary: one record per canvas-mount adapter request (INFO on `obtained`, WARN otherwise) behind its own exact allowlist leaf, carrying ONLY `{outcome (closed WebgpuAdapterOutcome enum; unknown rejected at deserialization), window_label (coerced 4+unknown)}`; the raw adapter / rejection error text is excluded by construction. Its procedure `telemetry.frontend.record_webgpu_adapter` is pinned in `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` with no capability-JSON change.

- `app.exit` (chunk 2026-10-01-conductor-return) is a deliberate NO-SCRUB product-originated log boundary: exactly one record per process end behind its own exact allowlist leaf beside `app.panic.fatal`, carrying ONLY `{exit_class, exit_code, exit_code_known, signal}` — two closed labels, an `i32` (0 when unknown), a bool; a panic payload, an error `Display`, a native message and every path are excluded by construction (re-exec arms: 0 full paths, 0 planted canary). Its stated failure mode is the set of ends it cannot see: SIGKILL, `_exit`, Windows `TerminateProcess`, a Rust `std::process::exit` on Windows (`ExitProcess`, no `atexit`), pre-sink failures. No TauRPC procedure, port or capability is involved.

- NEVER log, or run code that needs thread-locals, from a C `atexit` handler or a signal handler on the thread ending the process — glibc runs that thread's TLS destructors before `atexit` handlers, and a `LocalKey::with` panic in an `extern "C"` handler aborts. The `libc` exit FFI (`pulse-app/src/observability.rs`) hands off to a thread spawned at install (`pulse-exit-reporter`, a bounded wait), and the Unix signal path records from a runtime task, then restores `SIG_DFL` and re-raises the SAME signal — never an exit code standing in for it.

- The P-047 catalog is **8 categories** (JWT · bearer · api_key · secret_kv · **provider_key** · email · credit_card · ssn). `provider_key` (2026-08-22) is the BARE-credential arm: the four credential arms before it require a key name, so a standalone `sk_live_…` / `sk-proj-…` / `ghp_…` / `AKIA…` token matched nothing and was stored verbatim. It is anchored-prefix + length-floor — never entropy scoring, which false-positives on trace ids and hashes; the false-positive corpus in `crates/security/src/scrubber.rs` is what bounds it, so any new arm must keep ordinary high-entropy identifiers `Allowed`.

- The `credit_card` arm is **precision-gated** (chunk `2026-09-29-scrubber-path-false-positive`, founder-ratified). It matches a candidate run of ASCII digit groups joined by single ` `/`-` only when some window of consecutive WHOLE groups carrying 13–19 digits passes Luhn, so a date-time stamp (`rm-20260923-093840`, a harness data-dir basename) or a 19-digit nanosecond timestamp is `Allowed`. The accepted recall trade: a Luhn-invalid (mistyped) card number, or one fused into a longer single digit group, is not redacted. Windows are whole groups only, NEVER arbitrary digit offsets — a long digit run offers so many offset windows that most non-card runs would pass Luhn by chance.

- **Span-level masking, not whole-value replacement** (chunk `2026-09-30-span-level-redaction`, a Boundary widening the founder ratified at P4 2026-10-01, «Ок давай по типу правила»): every scrub site except `metrics_points.labels` calls `security::scrubber::mask_secret_spans(value, placeholder)`, which masks each secret where it sits and keeps the rest of the value byte-identical — one card number no longer blanks a digest. The extent is CLASS-AWARE and is what keeps never-weaken: keyed arms (`bearer` · `api_key` · `secret_kv`) mask from the key word to the END OF THE LINE (a multi-word value after `password:` or a base64 bearer tail past `+`/`/` lies outside the regex match); bare arms (`jwt` · `provider_key` · `email` · `ssn`) mask the whole whitespace-delimited token; `credit_card` masks the Luhn-qualifying digit-group run; overlapping or touching spans merge under the earliest arm in catalog order. `scrub_attribute` stays the detection VERDICT (it gates the mask; a flagged value with no locatable span masks whole — fail closed) and stays the only call at `encode_labels`. Masking re-runs to a bounded fixpoint (≤ 4 extra passes) because a mask can expose a match its neighbour hid (a Luhn-valid run fused to a key word). Each consumer passes its own placeholder spelling (`[REDACTED:{c}]` · `[redacted:{c}]` · `[redacted: {c}]`), never unify them in passing. A JSON payload is masked PER STRING LEAF, never as serialized text — `secret_kv`'s `\S+` runs across compact-JSON delimiters (`scrubbed_l4_json`, the training export's `interpretation`); a count of redacted fields looks for a placeholder ANYWHERE in the field, never at its start.

- **Scrubber coverage on the OTLP path is now complete for every column a producer can reach** (measured 2026-08-23): `log_records.body` · `exception_message` / `exception_stacktrace` on `span_events` + `log_records` · since chunk `2026-08-23-ingestion-scrub-coverage`, `spans.service_name` · `span_events.name` · `metrics_points.metric_name` · `log_records.severity_text` · and, since chunk `2026-08-23-metrics-points-labels`, a FIFTH cell `metrics_points.labels` (a data point's attribute set). **That fifth cell uses a THIRD scrub SHAPE** — the scrub input is the JOINED `key=value` form UNIONED with the bare value, because `secret_kv` and `api_key` are key-name-anchored and structurally unreachable on a split value: a label `{password: "hunter2"}` presents only `hunter2` to a value-only scrub and matches NOTHING, so the whole keyed class would store verbatim. Label KEYS are stored verbatim; only the VALUE becomes `[REDACTED:{category}]`, so two distinct keys never collapse into one placeholder. Accepted failure mode: over-redaction when the KEY alone trips a match (`password=1`), per the key-anchored arms' recall-over-precision posture. `service_name` is scrubbed INSIDE `extract_service_name`, not at the column push — that fn feeds three consumers (the `spans` column, the storm `FingerprintObserver`, the baseline `SpanObserver` tap) and scrubbing only the column would leave two raw paths into `triage` and desync DuckDB identity from the baseline registry. The tap drives one `CompositeSpanObserver` (baseline, restart, and since chunk `2026-09-30-p-027-discovery-bound` the first-sighting `DiscoveryObserverAdapter`), so its scrubbed name now also keys the lifecycle `ServiceRegistry` directly at a service's first span — the choke point still has THREE consumers; what grew is the tap's fan-out, and the desync argument covers the lifecycle registry too. `metrics_points.metric_name` is the one target inside a PRIMARY KEY. That collision is **CLOSED** since chunk `2026-08-23-metrics-points-identity`: the key gained a `seq` ordinal, so two distinct credential-shaped names redacting identically at the same `ts_unix_nano` + `resource_hash` no longer collide — both rows persist and no batch fails. The discriminator is content-INDEPENDENT (a per-table monotonic counter, never derived from the secret), so the rejected alternative still stands. **Residual:** two names that differ only inside a masked span still mask to one text (a multi-word name keeps its non-secret words under span masking), so those rows land indistinguishable — redaction holds and nothing new leaks, but the whole-batch ERROR was the only signal that such a collision had happened, and closing it removed that signal. Still NOT covered, by construction: `span_events.exception_type` (a DELIBERATE exclusion — class identifier, not user content). The producer-less `instrumentation_scopes` (with `resources` / `span_links`) no longer exists — its CREATE was deleted at chunk 2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep, so every reserved ring-buffer table has a producer and no scrub target is vacuous. The DuckDB ring buffer remains UNENCRYPTED, so redaction at the write boundary is the control, not confidentiality at rest. Before claiming a column is scrubbed, still check the call site.
- Self-observation runtime is `tracing` + `tracing-subscriber` JSON + `tracing-appender` daily file sink ONLY. NO OTel SDK linked into the product binary for self-observation.
- NEVER instrument the product's own telemetry with an OTLP network exporter pointed at the product's own `:4317`/`:4318` — infinite loop + bypasses loopback authorization model.
- Tauri updater Minisign Ed25519 verification cannot be disabled — never override.
- NEVER ship the Minisign **private** key in the repo or in any build artifact — only the public key belongs in `tauri.conf.json`.
- Windows EV signing cert lives in Azure Key Vault HSM (DigiCert / GlobalSign HSM-RSA only); key never leaves HSM.
- GitHub Actions reaches Azure Key Vault via OIDC federation — NEVER store a long-lived Azure service principal secret in GitHub Actions secrets.
- Pin every third-party GitHub Action by 40-char commit SHA: `<owner>/<repo>@<40-char-SHA> # vX.Y.Z`. NEVER `@v2` or floating tag (`tj-actions/changed-files` CVE-2025-30066, 23k repos).
- `permissions:` at workflow level MUST be `contents: read`; elevate per-job to `write` only on the publish step.
- All signing secrets, Apple Developer ID credentials, and Tauri updater private key MUST be in GitHub Environment `production-release` with manual approval gate.

- Run `cargo audit` + `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` in CI on every PR. The `bans` check catches the documented `tonic 0.14 ↔ opentelemetry-otlp 0.31 (pinned tonic 0.13)` duplicate. The `licenses` check covers the workspace's OWN crates as well as its dependencies — `deny.toml` sets no `private` key (measured 2026-09-30: a scratch config without `"MIT"` rejected all 16 members) — and the project's own `MIT OR Apache-2.0` passes because both `MIT` and `Apache-2.0` are in `[licenses] allow`. The npm channel has its own gate since `2026-08-30-npm-advisory-coverage`: `cargo xtask check:npm-supply-chain` (ci.yml `supply-chain` job; policy at `pulse-app/ui/npm-policy.json` — GHSA-scoped exceptions with mandatory provenance, per-class license allowlists, package-name denylist; lockfile-only, no `npm ci`; exit 0 green · 1 findings/policy red · 2 cannot-evaluate). The staged-artifacts channel since `2026-08-30-staged-bindings-assertion`: `cargo xtask check:staged-artifacts` (staged git-index bindings + capability grants vs `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` / `staged_gate::EXPECTED_GRANTS`; exit 0 staged-clean · 1 staged-drift · 2 cannot-evaluate; its own ci.yml step AND folded into capability-drift).

- `cargo audit` runs in CI as the plain step `run: cargo audit` of the `supply-chain` job (since chunk `2026-10-09-supply-chain-job-same-on-push-and-pull-request`) — no third-party action, no token input, no `continue-on-error`, on the runner image's own `cargo-audit`; exit 0 clean · 1 a vulnerability · 2 could not evaluate, red on 1 and on 2; pinned by `ci_workflow_audit_step_is_a_plain_run_step`. NEVER put it back behind an action that publishes a check run: under `permissions: contents: read` `rustsec/audit-check` failed a push on its own reporting while passing on a pull request.

- 2026-05-23: EXTENSION to the 2026-05-16 / 2026-05-18 / 2026-05-19 cross-crate state delivery family — handles ASYNC traits with `Arc<dyn Trait>` injection WITHOUT adding the `async-trait` workspace dep. Rust 1.85's native `async fn` in traits is NOT dyn-compatible by default (the implicit `impl Future` return is not object-safe via the `dyn` keyword unless wrapped through `#[trait_variant::make]` or `async-trait` macro). Workspace v0.2.0 chunks operate under a "Workspace deps delta: none" discipline (per pulse-v0_2_0-route §80 + analogous chunk callouts), so adding `async-trait` to enable a single trait's dyn-compat is over-cost. Resolution: declare async-trait methods with **manual `Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send + 'a>>` return types** — object-safe by construction, no macro magic, no extra dep:

Cost: one `Box::pin(async move { ... })` per method body (small allocation per call; acceptable for non-hot-path orchestration like cadence coordinator). Type alias `type SqlFuture<'a, T> = ...` keeps signatures readable. The `'a` lifetime on `&'a self` flows through to the future so the closure can borrow `&self.state`. - 2026-08-23: A REGEX CATALOG'S ARMS CAN REQUIRE THE COMPOSED FORM — scrubbing a DECOMPOSED value silently disables the key-anchored subset. `scrub_attribute` takes one `&str` and matches the whole 8-arm catalog against it, but two arms need the key name INSIDE that string: `secret_kv` is `(?i)(password|passwd|secret|token)[\s=:]+\S+` and `api_key` is `(?i)(api[_\-]?key|access[_\-]?token|secret[_\-]?key|auth[_\-]?token)[\s=:]+[\w\-]{12,}`. So any write boundary that takes a structured pair and scrubs the VALUE alone — a label set, an attribute map, a header list, a KV config blob — presents `hunter2` where the catalog expects `password=hunter2`, matches NOTHING, and stores the entire keyed class verbatim while the bare-shape arms (JWT, provider_key, email, credit_card, ssn) keep firing normally. The failure is invisible from the outside: the scrubber runs, a redaction counter still advances on the bare-shape hits, and only the keyed class leaks. **Rule for any new pair-shaped scrub site: pass the JOINED `key=value` string, and union it with the bare value so an `^`/`$`-anchored arm (none exist today) could not be missed either.** Redact by reconstructing `{key}=[REDACTED:{category}]` from the key you already hold — `ScrubbedValue::Redacted` carries a category and no content — which also keeps KEYS verbatim, so two distinct dimensions never collapse into one placeholder. Accept the resulting over-redaction when the KEY alone trips a match (`password=1`), per the key-anchored arms' recall-over-precision posture [corrected 2026-09-30: the posture is no longer catalog-wide — the `credit_card` arm is Luhn-gated since `2026-09-29-scrubber-path-false-positive`]. Verified at `2026-08-23-metrics-points-labels` (`metrics_points.labels`): the operator caught the value-only design at review, and the mutation check confirmed it — neutralising the joined-form scrub stores `password=hunter2` byte-for-byte. A RED leg carrying only a bare `sk_live_…` value would have passed while the keyed class leaked, so canary corpora for a pair-shaped site need BOTH classes.

- 2026-08-26: A CONTENT GUARD OVER STRUCTURED TEXT MUST WHITELIST ITS LAYOUT CHARACTERS — `char::is_control()` is TRUE for `\n`, `\r` and `\t`, so a "reject control characters" bound written the obvious way rejects every multi-line payload it is meant to protect. The failure is silent and total in the wrong direction: the guard does not leak, it DISABLES — a markdown prompt, a JSON document, an indented config or any newline-bearing value is refused, the feature stops working, and every negative test still passes because the rejection arms are exactly what the guard was written to do. Rule for any byte/char bound over a payload that is structured text: enumerate the characters the payload's own producer emits BY CONSTRUCTION, whitelist those explicitly (`c.is_control() && c != '\n' && c != '\r' && c != '\t'` is the in-repo form, used by both the L4 prompt bound and the stdout-snippet sanitiser), and pin a REALISTIC multi-line sample as ACCEPTED — not only a NUL-bearing one as rejected. The accept pin is the one carrying the guard: mutation-checked at `2026-08-26-l4-runtime-security-residuals`, dropping the whitelist reddened ONLY the accepts-multi-line test while all three rejection pins stayed green, which is the conditional-property asymmetry in its most consequential form.

- 2026-08-27: A WIRE-COMPAT CLAIM MUST NAME ITS CODEC — a `#[serde(default)]` + JSON round-trip test proves NOTHING for a bincode-persisted struct. `serde(default)` fills a missing field only under self-describing formats; bincode is positional, so ADDING a trailing field to a struct persisted as a bincode BLOB makes every pre-existing row undecodable — and in this codebase one undecodable row fails the WHOLE hydration (`bincode::deserialize::<Incident>(...).map_err(...)?` inside the `load_active_incidents` loop, `pulse-app/src/incident_persistence.rs`), so a "backward-compatible" field addition bricks boot restore for any corpus with history. The trap is that the compat test LOOKS right: `crates/triage/src/contract.rs`'s `incident_deserializes_pre_chunk_86_payload_without_resolution_summary_field` parses JSON, and passes forever while saying nothing about the BLOB codec. Discipline before changing any persisted struct's shape: grep the PERSIST site for the encode call (`bincode::serialize` vs `serde_json`) and treat the codec as the compat contract — prefer FIELD REUSE with a semantics-broadening doc (the chunk `2026-08-26-interpretation-brief-completeness` resolution: `resolution_summary_text` became "latest interpretation, resolution is the final write", zero wire change, and the cross-process MCP sidecar picked the behavior up purely from data), else a versioned decode shim; never a bare field addition justified by a JSON test. Pairs with the 2026-06-01 cross-process bincode-config-parity entry (same substrate, different facet: that one is CONFIG parity, this one is SHAPE evolution).

- 2026-08-27: ARGV-TRANSPORTED TEMPLATE TEXT STAYS ASCII — llama.cpp's b9305 Windows build decodes argv through ANSI `main(argc, argv)`, so any non-ASCII character in a prompt TEMPLATE crosses the boundary as an active-codepage byte (U+2014 → lone 0x97, invalid standalone UTF-8) and can come back in the subprocess's stdout, failing `String::from_utf8` on the whole generation. The poisoning subset is NARROWER than "any non-ASCII in the prompt": schema-description prose (`§`, `≤`) rode every v2.2 prompt through 3,678 clean generations because the model never echoes it, while the ONE em-dash in the reflection ROLE text — instruction phrasing the model PARAPHRASES into its output fields — failed 22/22 reflection generations for 11h as a then-silent `InferenceFailed`. So the rule is template-wide anyway (the echo subset is model-dependent and not worth relitigating per character): keep ALL prompt template text ASCII — role definitions, reminders, runtime-pushed literals, AND the embedded `schema.json` descriptions — pinned by `composed_prompt_templates_are_ascii_clean_for_argv_transport` (`crates/interpretation/src/prompt.rs`), which proved its own discrimination by failing against real remaining content on first run. Distinct from the 2026-08-26 layout-chars entry above: that one whitelists control characters in a REJECT guard; this one bans non-ASCII in the CONTENT because the defect is the OS argv decode, which no in-process guard sees. Root-caused + live-fixed at `2026-08-27-idle-observer-generation-damper` (the fix produced the project's first successful reflection generation).

- 2026-08-27: A TAURI CAPABILITY'S RUNTIME ACL CANNOT BE PROBED BY `strings` ON ITS `description` — the field is DOCUMENTATION and Tauri strips it from the ACL compiled into the binary, so a grep for text you just added returns 0 whether the build is fresh or stale. The failure is a false NEGATIVE that reads as confirmation: it says "the grant is not in the binary" in both worlds, so it can appear to corroborate a staleness hypothesis and then keep appearing to corroborate it after a clean rebuild has already fixed things. Two probes that DO discriminate: read the build-generated `target/{profile}/build/pulse-app-*/out/capabilities.json` (the resolved `windows` + `permissions` per capability, which is what the ACL is compiled from), and — decisive — exercise the permission at runtime and read the rejection, contrasting a window the grant already covered against the one under test in the SAME run. Measured at `2026-08-27-report-window-copy-affordance`: `report` returned `Command plugin:clipboard-manager|write_text not allowed by ACL` while `compact-widget` returned OK, which is what localized the fault away from the capability file. Generalizes to any compiled-in manifest whose human-readable fields are dropped at build time — probe the resolved artifact or the behaviour, never the prose.

- 2026-08-28: A LEGITIMATE REFUSAL IS A RETURN VALUE, NOT AN ERROR — and the call-site shape decides how badly getting this wrong hurts. When a write/guard can decline for a reason that is EXPECTED rather than faulty (a stale write losing to a fresher one, a conditional update matching no row on purpose), encoding the refusal as an `Err` variant makes "log it as a failure" the DEFAULT at every call site: existing callers written as `if let Err(err) = …` bind only the error arm, so each one silently starts reporting a normal outcome as a fault, and nothing in the type system asks them to reconsider. Returning an outcome enum instead (`Applied` | `DeclinedStale`) forces each caller to acknowledge the second case while leaving genuine errors — the row does not exist — in the `Err` arm where they belong. The counting corollary: fold the refusals as an aggregate on the operation's existing per-cycle record rather than logging per refusal, since a systematically-declining row would otherwise flood the log. NOTE the cross-crate half — when the mirroring trait sits BELOW the owning crate in the dependency DAG, declare a PARALLEL enum in the lower crate and map between them in the binary-boundary adapter; a re-export would invert the DAG. This joins the cross-crate delivery family above (trait-in-lower-crate · free-fn `map_err` · N-trait-from-one-`Arc` · async `Pin<Box>` · bounded-`String` label) as its return-TYPE sibling. Verified at `2026-08-27-incident-persist-vs-resolve-write-race`: seven production writers share one guarded corpus write, six of them already binding only the `Err` arm — so the value-typed outcome was what kept a declined write off the error target without touching those six.

- 2026-08-29: `cargo tree -i <crate>` ANSWERS FOR THE HOST TARGET ONLY — a dependency-parent claim derived from it silently excludes target-gated holders, and `--target all` (or the lockfile itself) is the graph-wide basis. Measured at `2026-08-29-advisory-backlog`: research mapped quick-xml 0.39.2's sole parent as `plist` from a host-target inverse tree; after updating plist the copy SURVIVED — the second holder was the Linux-only wayland clipboard chain (`tauri-plugin-clipboard-manager → arboard → wl-clipboard-rs → wayland-scanner`), invisible on Windows, found only by re-running with `--target all`. The empty variant is worse: a host-target `cargo tree -i` on a purely foreign-target dep prints "nothing to print", which reads as "no dependents" when the truth is "no dependents ON THIS TARGET". Rule for any advisory/upgrade/dedup work that reasons about who pulls a crate: derive holder sets with `--target all`, or grep `Cargo.lock` directly — and treat a survivor after a parent bump as evidence of an unmapped holder, not a failed update.

- 2026-08-30: `npm audit`'s `fixAvailable` FIELD IS RESOLVER OUTPUT, NOT UPGRADE GUIDANCE — its named target can drift between consecutive runs and can point at a major DOWNGRADE, and a bare `true` can stand against a range where no in-range fix exists. Measured at `2026-08-30-npm-advisory-coverage`: the webdriverio cluster's suggested "fix" moved 8.14.6 → 7.40.0 (two majors BACKWARD) across runs, and lighthouse read `fixAvailable: true` while its entire installed major was inside the vulnerable range (the real fix was the next major). Rule for npm disposition work: never plan upgrades from `fixAvailable` — measure with `npm audit fix --dry-run`, then APPLY and re-audit (the residual is the truth); treat a downgrade-shaped suggestion as "no forward fix" (exception-with-closing-condition class, never a downgrade of a harness driver). Extended 2026-09-30: when a transitive advisory's patched release lies inside every dependent's semver range, first confirm the release exists with `npm view {pkg} versions`, then close it with a targeted `npm update {pkg}`. That moves only those lockfile entries and leaves `package.json` untouched. Extended 2026-10-01: when every dependent's range EXCLUDES the patched major (no upgrade path reaches it), check that the API the dependent actually calls is unchanged in the patched major, then pin it with a `package.json` `overrides` entry and prove it with `npm audit` plus `check:npm-supply-chain`; take a documented exception only when no fixed path exists at all.

- 2026-08-30: `package-lock.json` IS THE CANONICAL ENUMERATION FOR npm SUPPLY-CHAIN TOOLING — its entries carry `license` fields (906/909 coverage measured here) and `dev` class flags, so license and dependency-class checks read the COMMITTED lockfile alone: deterministic across environments, no `npm ci` needed, and it covers platform-conditional optional packages that are never installed on the current host. A blind `node_modules` walk is the wrong basis twice over — it hits name-less nested test-fixture stubs (measured: `test-fixtures`/`baz`/`browser_field` inside installed packages) and misses the non-installed platform variants. The few field-less lockfile entries become explicit policy exceptions, never silent skips.

- 2026-09-29: CI's Node/npm MAJOR must match the host that writes `pulse-app/ui/package-lock.json` — npm 10 and npm 11 disagree on unmet OPTIONAL peers, so `npm ci` under npm 10 refuses a lock npm 11 wrote (the host runs npm 11, so CI runs Node 24).

- 2026-10-10: Harness code that runs INSIDE the product's process (a preloaded library, an injected hook) is never classed routine harness evidence on the operator's reading alone: record its classification PROVISIONAL, name the reading and its date, and leave the class to the founder's own word. A harness-only variable the product's own code never reads is a different class and keeps its own rule.

paths:
  - "crates/**/src/**/*.rs"
  - "pulse-app/**/*.rs"
  - "xtask/**/*.rs"
  - "tests/**/*.rs"

---
Path-scoped rules for Rust source + colocated test modules + webview frontend tests. Loaded only when Claude is working with files matching the `paths:` frontmatter above.
**Authoritative source:** `.andromeda/test-plan.md` §3 (Test Harness Contract) + §6 (E2E P1–P7) + §10 (Quality Gates) + §11 (Anti-Patterns). Tier=Standard.

- **Unit tests (Rust):** `cargo test` (libtest, the pinned rustc 1.95.0; the declared `rust-version = "1.95"` equals the pin — the dependency graph sets it, the workspace's own code needs ≥ 1.89 — witnessed by `declared_floor_equals_the_pinned_channel`) + `cargo-nextest` 0.9.x for per-process isolation (port-binding tests need this; it separates processes, not port numbers — a port bound to 0, read and released can be handed to another test starting at the same instant, so the port-using suites — the spawned ones and the in-process arms of `integration_engine_boot.rs` — claim their ports through the one `test_support::ports::claim_port`, under an advisory file lock in `target/test-ports/`).

- **Unit tests (webview, since chunk #11):** `vitest` 4.x (4.1.11 since chunk 2026-09-29-p-025-hue-shift-observable-made-gradable; the vitest 3 mocker is vulnerable, GHSA-82fw) with `jsdom` 26 environment + `@testing-library/react` 16 for DOM-shape assertions on React 19 components. Co-located `*.test.tsx` adjacent to source under `pulse-app/ui/src/`. Emits JUnit XML to `target/junit-ui.xml` (matches `cargo-nextest --message-format junit` shape) for agent-driven discipline. Coverage gate scope: presentational components (e.g., `pulse-app/ui/src/components/icons/`) explicitly EXCLUDED at Foundation pre-shell stage; integration coverage applies via `tauri-driver` E2E from chunk #25 (webview shell). `vitest.config.mjs` lives at `pulse-app/ui/vitest.config.mjs` with `setupFiles: ["./src/test-setup.ts"]` registering `@testing-library/react` `afterEach(cleanup)`.
- **Integration tests:** `cargo nextest run --filter-expr 'integration'` with `#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]` for concurrent OTLP ingest tests.

- **E2E desktop-webview:** `@crabnebula/tauri-driver` 2.x + `webdriverio` 9.x, invoked by `cargo xtask webview-drive [--expect-absent <STAGE>] [--no-inject]` — **no `mocha` and no `@wdio/*` runner is installed** (measured 2026-08-23). Drives a **17-stage** assembled path under deterministic-L4 (7 → 13 at 2026-08-23-headful-leg-extension, 13 → 15 at 2026-08-24-headful-mechanics-probe-race-disposition, 15 → 16 at 2026-08-27-report-window-copy-affordance, whose `report-copy` presses the report's real Copy control and reads its settled `data-copy-state`, 16 → 17 at 2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep, whose DOM-only `boot-geometry` re-derives the app's own snap formula from the recorded widget/monitor geometry + scale — the 2026-08-24 mechanics probe DECLINED a drag and a resize stage on measurement — W3C pointer Actions and `setWindowRect` reach the WRY window and produce zero delta; blank-webview victims of the automation-environment navigation race are re-navigated at launch and recorded in `recovered_from_blank`) (the gate is set into the driver's spawn env, since the app is a grandchild process); telemetry enters only over real OTLP via `crates/ingest/examples/inject_demo`. The `.mjs` driver drives and REPORTS only — it asserts nothing, emitting DOM observations to a per-run TempDir `webview-drive-stages.json`; the assertions and verdict live in `xtask/src/webview_drive.rs`, which reports each stage as two independent halves (obs / DOM) and reads the app's own obs log. `msedgedriver` is located via `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MSEDGEDRIVER_PATH` and must match the installed WebView2 Runtime (unset ⇒ clean SKIP, exit 0). Headful agent-driven GUI automation is IN scope; canvas pixel inspection remains OUT.
- **E2E TauRPC IPC:** `tauri::test::mock_builder()` + `get_ipc_response()` (in-process, fast).

- **E2E OTLP gRPC:** `tonic` 0.14.5 native client → loopback `:4317`. **OTLP HTTP:** `reqwest` 0.12.x async + `axum-test` 18.7.0 → loopback `:4318`. **MCP tools (P3):** no stdio sidecar, no `mcp-server` feature and no env gate — a `tokio::net::UnixStream` client writes JSON-RPC 2.0 lines to the door of a spawned `andromeda-pulse-engine run` (`pulse-app/tests/e2e_p3_mcp_subprocess_tools_call.rs`; the door below). **Console engine program:** the built `andromeda-pulse-engine` spawned by `std::process::Command` from `pulse-app/tests/integration_console_engine.rs` under a cleared environment (no display variable, no session bus, its own TempDir data dir, two claimed loopback ports — since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed a number from 20000 to 31999, 24317 and 24318 left out, held under an advisory file lock in `target/test-ports/`, never bound to 0 and released), its command grammar in process through `pulse-app/tests/unit_console_commands.rs`; the harness's own path to it is `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle` on ports 24317 / 24318; and since that chunk the committed `scripts/agent-run.sh` and the built cycle verb are run with `bash` on a real console engine by the two `xtask/tests` binaries (`agent_run_shell`, `engine_cycle_refusals`), which need `bash`, a Linux `/proc` and the engine built in the test profile. **Console engine door (Unix only):** a `tokio::net::UnixStream` client at `{data dir}/run/door/sock` — over a stand-in `Tools` in process (`unit_door.rs`), the door seated by `engine_boot::start` in process (`integration_engine_boot.rs`) and a spawned `andromeda-pulse-engine run` (`integration_door.rs`) — and, since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door, the stdio relay `andromeda-pulse-engine door` (`unit_door_bridge.rs` and two relay arms of `integration_door.rs`); the two other-account arms print a skip sentence and pass where `sudo -n true` fails, so the `lint-test` step `Door refuses another account` runs both on the runner and fails unless it reads both arms' sentences (PROVISIONAL with the door).

- **Rust:** co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { … }` within each LIBRARY crate's `src/` (no separate `tests/` directory per arch convention). **`pulse-app` is the exception** — its `[lib] test = false` (the Windows WebView2 load workaround) makes a src-level `mod tests` compile under clippy but NEVER run, so pulse-app's unit-shaped probes go in `pulse-app/tests/*.rs` (112 files, as measured at the work tree of chunk 2026-11-03-stdio-sidecar-retired; 112 at chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process) and reach internals via `pub` + `#[doc(hidden)]`. A probe placed in `pulse-app/src/` cannot fail and is not a guard — and since chunk 2026-08-30-dead-lib-src-test-migration the state is a FLAT ZERO: `LEGACY_DEAD_BASELINE` is EMPTY, so any `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` in a pulse-app lib source reds the ratchet (`main.rs` a `[[bin]]` exemption holding one test, `emit_taurpc_bindings`; the package's second `[[bin]]`, `src/bin/andromeda-pulse-engine.rs`, carries none). **`xtask/tests/` is the second separate tests directory** since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed: two integration binaries (`agent_run_shell.rs`, `engine_cycle_refusals.rs`) over a shared `xtask/tests/common/mod.rs`, because they drive the committed script, the built `harness:engine-cycle` verb and the built engine as processes; xtask's unit pins stay co-located in `xtask/src`. `check:english-sources` and `quarantine-tracking` read the directory, and its absence fails both.
- **Webview:** co-located `*.test.tsx` adjacent to source under `pulse-app/ui/src/`. Vitest discovers via `include: ["src/**/*.{test,spec}.{ts,tsx}"]` per `pulse-app/ui/vitest.config.mjs`.
- Test fixtures (pre-compiled WASM Component Model binaries): `tests/fixtures/plugins/` (committed to repo, shared read-only per suite).
- Property-based regression files: `proptest-regressions/` (committed for replay).
- Every test MUST exit with a deterministic signal (exit code 0/non-zero, structured JSON, log-line match) — no human-in-the-loop, no visual inspection, no Percy/Chromatic.
- Self-bootstrapping fixtures: tests seed their own data via OTLP ingest through the live receiver — NO pre-baked DuckDB snapshots, NO `.sql` scripts.

- Synthetic data generators: one set of factories, `test_support::otlp` in the dev-only member `crates/test-support` (`span_event()`, `span()`, `metric_point()`, `gauge()`, `log_record()`, `resource()`; since chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data) — event time, service and string attributes settable, every default fixed, no clock, nothing random. `buffer`, `pulse-app` and `xtask` take it as a dev-dependency; a unit module of `ingest` cannot (the member depends on `ingest`; reasoned, not measured by a compile). There is no `MockTraceSpan` / `MockArrowBatch` / `MockMetricPoint` and no Arrow-batch factory: test-plan §3 item 6 dropped them. Tests the set does not yet serve seed via OTLP ingest through the live receiver, per-test in-memory DuckDB inserts, and `rstest` fixtures.
- Per-test isolation: `tempfile::TempDir` + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR=$TMPDIR/test-$$` + ephemeral in-memory DuckDB (`duckdb::open_in_memory()`).
- Deterministic time: `tokio::time::pause()` + `tokio::time::advance(Duration)` for retention-window tests; NEVER `std::time::Instant::now()` / `chrono::Utc::now()` without injection.
- AAA pattern visible per test; one assertion concept per test.
- NEVER mock the OTLP receiver under test — use live `tonic` client / `reqwest` against loopback.
- NEVER mock DuckDB at integration level — use ephemeral `duckdb::open_in_memory()` per test.
- NEVER mock `tokio` / `tonic` / framework internals — mock only traits you own (`mockall` 0.13.x with `#[automock]`).
- Time mocking: built-in `tokio::time::pause()` only.
- HTTP mock for `tauri-plugin-updater` `latest.json`: `httpmock` 0.7.x (fallback `mockito` 1.6.x); valid + invalid Minisign signatures.
- Property-based: `proptest` 1.10.0 with seed control.

title: Critical paths (E2E P1–P7) — must each pass

data.head: ## Critical paths (E2E P1–P7) — must each pass

body: - **P1** Receive OTLP gRPC → buffer → `traces.query` returns rows.
- **P2** `snapshot.generate({token_budget: 25000})` → markdown with anomaly markers + `token_count <= 25000` + `dedup_count > 0` + p50/p95/p99 aggregates.
- **P3** MCP `tools/call` with `query_traces` returns array of trace objects.
- **P4** Plugin lifecycle: load WASM → `plugins.list` → `plugins.invoke({capability})` → negative test on disallowed capability.

- **P5** Widget ↔ dashboard ↔ tray — proven agent-side by the 17-stage headful leg (`cargo xtask webview-drive`), whose `widget-close` stage (no longer terminal — `signpost-repeat` follows it to prove the toast fires on EVERY close) requires the `ui.layout.transition {compact-widget → hidden}` record AND the `tray.signpost.shown` record with `window_label == "compact-widget"` after a real press; a driver-side resize stage is DECLINED on measurement (`setWindowRect` returns cleanly with zero delta); tray-icon repaint and OS-notification delivery remain IPC-surrogate, deferred to the headful suite. Two RED arms, not equivalent: telemetry-suppression is code (`--no-inject --expect-absent <STAGE>`), capability-revoke is still by hand (one revoke cycle reddens five stages).
- **P6** Subscribe to `pulse://stream/spans` → ingest gRPC trace → receive Arrow IPC payload → schema match.
- **P7** `workspace.detect()` returns `{project_name, root_path, vcs_type: "git", vcs_root}`.

- Coverage: ≥75% line, ≥85% function via `cargo-llvm-cov` 0.8.5 (LLVM source-based; in CI it runs in the `coverage` job on `ubuntu-22.04`, the workflow's one runner system). The ≥70% branch threshold is RETIRED as never measured — PROVISIONAL, on the operator's reading of 2026-10-10, awaiting the founder's own word: the arm read `0/0 = 100.0%` on every run, because a branch count needs a compiler channel the project does not pin (nightly-only `-Z coverage-options=branch`); it returns when that is stable on the pinned channel or the founder admits a second channel, with a measured first reading before any threshold. A coverage report tracking 0 lines or 0 functions fails the step, and so does an absent `lcov.info` (chunk 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing; the step's script is run by four witness tests, which need `bash` and `awk` on PATH). Exclude generated code (`prost` stubs, `taurpc` IPC bindings) and test fixtures. `xtask/` is excluded from the measure TEMPORARILY (founder ruling 2026-09-29, `COVERAGE_IGNORE_FILENAME_REGEX`) until the next epoch-boundary code audit revisits coverage quality, thresholds above 85 % and xtask's re-inclusion (test-plan §10). `crates/test-support` (test fixtures) stands INSIDE the measure since chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data, against test-plan §10's fixtures exclusion; the route entry `Scenario legs driven against the console engine` takes it out.

- Performance budgets (p99): OTLP gRPC Export <100ms, OTLP HTTP POST <120ms, TauRPC `traces.query` <150ms, Snapshot 25k budget <500ms, DuckDB Arrow appender <50ms, WebGPU 10k spans/sec sustained ≥30 fps (descriptive intent — the ASSERTED frame budget is obs-plan §10's ms-form, `metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms` p99 ≤33ms; no test asserts an fps number, and a frame PASS comes only from the dev-host `cargo xtask perf:frame-sample` — on CI the frame arm reads 0 samples and prints the named cannot-evaluate line, never PASS (test-plan §10 Frame-budget assertion)).

- **Capability record gate:** `docs/capability-record.json` is the one current record of all 82 capability ids P-001–P-082, each `claimed` or `retired` (36 claimed, 46 retired, as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-capability-record-re-based). `cargo xtask verify:capability-matrix` reads it and `andromeda-pulse-0.4.0/working-route.md` (two fixed paths, no argument, no environment variable), exit 0 clean · 1 findings · 2 cannot-evaluate, and runs in CI `lint-test` after `capability-widening-check`. It holds all 82 ids to the form and validates the proofs of claimed ids only (file refs exist, `contains` anchors found, a `note` on every `by-construction` / `external` / `manual` scenario); a retired entry names its surface, a working-route entry title that removes it and its guard, and carries no proof. The id set is closed in `xtask/src/capability_record.rs`: a change of it lands in the module and the record in the same chunk. A route-resolve that renames, retires or splits an entry the record names reddens the verb and the pin `the_committed_record_reads_clean_over_the_committed_route` until the record is corrected. The two older records (`docs/v0_2_0/capability-verification-matrix.json`, `andromeda-pulse-0.3.0/verification-matrix.json`) are superseded and read by no gate.

- **Four-profile load suite (chunk #99, release/tag gate):** `pulse-app/tests/perf_load_profiles.rs` implements the dist-arch v3 profiles {baseline 1k/60s zero-drops; high 10k×5min L1a p99<500ms; burst 50k/30s ≤60s recovery; sustained-extreme 50k×5min zero-L0-loss + retention}. Runs ONLY behind nextest `[profile.load-profiles]` (`test-threads = 1`; 20-min terminate ceiling; the default/ci profiles exclude the binary via `default-filter`), orchestrated by `cargo xtask perf:load-profiles`. Future load-shaped tests JOIN this profile rather than using `#[ignore]` (`#[ignore]` stays reserved for flake quarantine). `perf_slo_10k_spans.rs` remains the fast per-PR gate. A second opt-in profile, `[profile.perf-samples]`, selects `pulse-app/tests/perf_budget_samples.rs` — the in-process producer of the memory + snapshot samples that CI's `cargo xtask perf:budget --require memory,snapshot` grades on lint-test Linux (a sample source, not a load profile); the default profile excludes both binaries.
- **Zero-flakiness budget:** flaky tests are NOT tolerated. Quarantine immediately via `#[ignore]` + open issue; root-cause + fix or delete before unquarantining. NO retry-once policies.
- `cargo deny check bans` blocks `multiple-versions = "deny"` regressions (catches `tonic` 0.14/0.13 duplicate).

- NEVER `sleep(N)` for sync — wait for explicit signal: poll `health` TauRPC (`subsystems.buffer.rows_ingested >= N`), Channel event subscription, or — for a booted product process — the `cargo xtask harness:ready` verdict for the program asked (status `running-healthy` AND, on each resolved OTLP port, a TCP connection accepted that this run's own log shows bound; an accepting port with no bound record of this run reads `foreign`, not ready); a spawned program is read ready from both ports accepting, its records awaited by target under a bound. The pid file is not a readiness signal: both programs write the same path.
- NEVER share mutable state across parallel tests — each test gets `TempDir` + in-memory DuckDB.

- ~~NEVER allow OTLP self-dialing — negative test asserts product cannot be configured to dial own `:4317`/`:4318`.~~ **DEPRECATED** — by-construction-satisfied per obs-plan.md `2026-05-02 — Phase 3.5 pivot to tracing-only self-observation`: no OTel SDK in self-observation runtime → no exporter to misconfigure → no `ANDROMEDA_OBSERVER_URL`-shaped configuration surface exists → trigger is unimplementable. `/andromeda-implement` MUST treat this trigger as no-op (do NOT generate dead test code). The `ANDROMEDA_OBSERVER_URL` "must never exist" architectural guard remains in `gotchas.md` §Self-observation. The body sites in test-plan.md (§1 entity row `Self-observation loop prevention`, §1 trigger row `No self-OTLP dialing`, §11 Project-specific bullet) now read `by-construction-satisfied` — no test generated, no negative test required; the deprecation history lives in test-plan-amendments.md. Per amendments `2026-05-08T17-28-26Z-deprecate-self-otlp-loop-test` (`.andromeda/runs/2026-05-08T17-28-26-spec-amendment-deprecate-self-otlp-loop-test/amendment.md`; Decisions Log only) + `2026-05-08T21-00-00-obs-pivot-test-bodies` (`.andromeda/runs/2026-05-08T21-00-00-spec-amendment-obs-pivot-test-bodies/amendment.md`; the by-construction text stands at test-plan.md §1 (entity row + trigger row) and §11 Project-specific).
- NEVER assert "raw OTLP JSON dump" passes as snapshot — must show dedup count + anomaly markers + p50/p95/p99 aggregates.
- NEVER skip post-`prost` invariant negative tests — span_id != 8 bytes / trace_id != 16 bytes must reject without panic.
- NEVER assert receiver bound to non-loopback succeeds — security model invariant.

body: The following triggers are decided-and-recommended. Groups marked **LANDED** have shipped and are kept for the audit trail; `boot-smoke-coverage` and `chunk-gate-baseline-coverage` are already active disciplines (test-plan §3 "Per-chunk gate discipline"); a RETIRED group is kept for audit only; anything else stays deferred to the next `/andromeda-tests` re-run with this rule file as input. /andromeda-implement should NOT generate placeholder tests for these triggers; instead, the triggers require dedicated harness design (xtask test command + fixture pattern) that exceeds delta-rerun scope.

- **LANDED (chunk #77 — 2026-05-22):** PII vector test gaps (security plan §Logging vectors 2/3/4/6 lack explicit triggers; test plan currently only covers vector 5):

Materialized at `pulse-app/tests/security_apperror_sanitization.rs`.

Materialized at `pulse-app/tests/security_mcp_response_body_redaction.rs` (no feature gate: it calls `query_traces` through the door of a spawned console engine and asserts the marker 0 times in the engine's log family).

- **LANDED (chunk #77 — 2026-05-22):** Capability widening static analysis gap (security plan §API Anti-Patterns 3 NEVER-widen bans; current xtask capability-drift only checks TauRPC↔capability sync, not permission widening):
  - **[LANDED chunk #77]** `security-vector-coverage: Capability widening static analysis` — xtask test that parses each `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` and asserts: (a) `pulse:notification` contains only outbound emit permissions (no input handlers); (b) `pulse:tray` contains only outbound menu/icon permissions (no incoming-event handlers); (c) `pulse:plugin-fs` permissions limited to read of resolved plugin dir, no write/delete/execute, never exposed to webview JavaScript. Test fails with named permission and capability on widening detection. Materialized as new xtask sub-command `capability-widening-check` at `xtask/src/main.rs` (Cmd::CapabilityWideningCheck variant; mirrors existing capability-drift shape).
  - Per amendment `2026-05-08T17-28-29Z-document-capability-widening-test-gap` (`.andromeda/runs/2026-05-08T17-28-29-spec-amendment-document-capability-widening-test-gap/amendment.md`).
