- 2026-08-23: THE "NEVER CLICKS" GAP IS CLOSED FOR ONE LEG — `cargo xtask webview-drive` presses a real production control in the live Tauri window and asserts the app's OWN `ui.layout.transition {layout_mode_from: compact-widget, layout_mode_to: hidden}` record. **This narrows, but does not retire, the 2026-06-30 self-verify-never-clicks entry above:** `cargo xtask self-verify` still never clicks (it is boot-quit by construction), so the two harnesses are complementary — self-verify proves the shell boots, webview-drive proves one affordance is alive. Three things about the shape are load-bearing and generalize to any future affordance leg. (a) **The driver must not own the verdict.** The `.mjs` presses and asserts NOTHING; the assertion lives in `xtask/src/webview_drive.rs` reading the obs log. A press that "returned without throwing" is not evidence — the ACL drops a webview IPC silently, which is the exact dead-affordance mode this exists to catch, and it was reproduced live: with the grant revoked the button was still FOUND and still PRESSED successfully, and only the log showed nothing happened. (b) **Match the effect record, never the target alone** — boot also emits `ui.layout.transition` (`boot_default → top-right`), so a target-only match passes on a record the press did not cause. (c) **The RED arm is MANUAL and stays a one-time discrimination proof, not a per-run gate:** only `--expect-absent` is code; the revoke → rebuild → press → restore cycle is by hand, so "`capabilities/default.json` byte-identical after restore" is a DISCIPLINE **[corrected 2026-08-30: the grants half is now GATED — `staged_gate::EXPECTED_GRANTS` asserts the staged `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` semantic triple `{identifier, windows, permissions}` in BOTH directions (folded into `capability-drift` + the `check:staged-artifacts` verb, chunk 2026-08-30-staged-bindings-assertion), so a left-REVOKED or silently-ADDED grant reds CI mechanically; the test-plan trigger's grants half is discharged and only AUTOMATING the revoke-cycle itself remains by hand]**. Corollary for authoring any new leg: a green-on-arrival regression guard MUST be mutation-checked, or it guards nothing. **[extended 2026-08-23-integration-ux-e2e-test, corrected 2026-08-24, corrected again 2026-08-25, and again 2026-08-27: the leg is now SIXTEEN stages (13 → 15 at 2026-08-24-headful-mechanics-probe-race-disposition; 15 → 16 at 2026-08-27-report-window-copy-affordance, which added `report-copy` after `report-window` — a DOM-only stage pressing the report's real Copy control, which also DECLINED a drag and a resize stage on a measured probe and ended widget-close's run as the terminal stage — signpost-repeat follows it), widget-close's obs half requires the transition AND the `tray.signpost.shown` record with its `window_label` field, and `allow-close` is guarded by five stages, not one — two of the original three points sharpened.]** (a) still holds and got its general form: report each stage as **two independent halves — `obs` (the app's own record) and `dom` (what the driver saw), `None` where a half does not apply** — because a single combined boolean cannot say whether telemetry failed to LAND or merely failed to reach the SCREEN, which is the first question a red stage raises; the split diagnosed three of that chunk's six defects in one run each. (b) proved itself live in the direction that matters: the close predicate correctly REJECTED a `main → hidden` record when the wrong window's ✕ was pressed — a target-only match on `ui.layout.transition` would have reported a green `widget-close` that never touched the widget. And the dead-affordance mode has a SECOND cause beyond a missing ACL grant: **occlusion**. A focus-trapping modal left open on the same window swallowed the close press, producing exactly `dom:yes obs:NO` — control found, accessible name read, click returned, app did nothing. Dismiss modal state before pressing anything else on that surface, and never read "the click did not throw" as evidence.

- 2026-08-23: AUTHORING A STAGED HEADFUL DRIVER — three traps measured in one chunk, none of which the product caused. **(1) A mode gate must ride the spawn env of the process that actually launches the app.** The app under test is a GRANDCHILD (`xtask` → `node` → `tauri-driver` → app), so `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` set in the caller's shell never reaches it; the L4 path then attempts real model inference, finds no model, and no incident forms — indistinguishable from a broken storm→incident seam, and a failure that gets debugged against innocent product code. Set the gate into the driver's spawn env. **(2) NEVER re-invoke a toggling action inside a poll.** `openDashboard()` called from within `pollUntil` pressed the "Toggle dashboard" control every 250 ms for 30 s — ~120 presses — so whether the dashboard ended up open was decided by which parity the deadline landed on. Runs differed for exactly this reason and it reads as environmental flakiness. Press once, THEN poll for the effect. **(3) Identify a window or surface by an INVARIANT marker, never a route-conditional one.** The widget-vs-dashboard exclusion keyed on the trace table — which exists only on `/traces` — so once an earlier stage navigated the dashboard to `/logs`, the dashboard stopped matching its own exclusion and got picked as the widget; the app then correctly logged `main → hidden`. Key on something the surface always has (the tab nav), and when the DOM cannot disambiguate, read the real Tauri window label via `globalThis.__TAURI_INTERNALS__?.metadata?.currentWindow?.label` — `App.tsx` renders `<Dashboard />` for BOTH `main` and the `unknown` fallback, so URL + marker presence genuinely cannot separate them while the SPA is mounting. Traps (2) and (3) were **latent flakes that would have shipped**, on the suite's highest flake-risk surface, against a zero-flakiness budget. Corollary: build the diagnostics INTO the harness (a per-handle dump of label + URL + marker presence; a dump of the record family a failed stage expected) — each converted a run that said only "absent" into one that named the cause, and a harness that cannot report what it saw is the failure class these legs exist to close.

- 2026-08-23: ATTRIBUTE AN INTERMITTENT FAILURE BY SAMPLING **BOTH** SIDES BEFORE BLAMING THE CHANGE — and rebuild the artifact the tier under test actually consumes. A leg that fails several runs in a row under your change, and passed once without it, looks deterministic and is the natural moment to conclude "I broke it". Measured at `2026-08-23-a11y-verification`: three consecutive `cargo xtask webview-drive` failures with the chunk's changes against ONE baseline pass read as a confirmed regression — and it was wrong. Stashing the source, rebuilding the frontend, re-embedding the binary and sampling the baseline properly gave 3/3 failures there too; the flake was pre-existing. The discipline: (a) an n=1 baseline can never establish attribution for an intermittent failure — sample the other side at comparable n before writing the conclusion anywhere durable; (b) for a compiled or bundled tier, the source revert is not the experiment — the artifact the runner loads must be rebuilt too, or you have sampled your own change twice (the same trap voids a mutation check: a Playwright arm reads `ui/dist`, so a mutation left unbuilt passes and reads as "this pin does not discriminate"); (c) report the tally per condition rather than a verdict, because the numbers survive re-reading and the verdict does not. Once attributed, a flake in a leg outside the chunk's scope is SURFACED with its measured rates, never quietly fixed or quietly ignored. **[extended 2026-08-25 — the cheapest recipe, measured]** For a HARNESS regression specifically, `git stash push -- <only the harness files you touched>` restores the pristine driver in seconds and one run decides attribution; the app binary is NOT stashed, so the experiment isolates exactly the harness delta (the artifact-rebuild caveat above still governs the other direction). Run it BEFORE the second speculative fix, not after the third: at `2026-08-24-headful-mechanics-probe-race-disposition`, 3 failures with ZERO baseline samples read as "the leg needs a bigger budget" and drove three useless ceiling raises, while one pristine run (184s PASS) reclassified it as a self-inflicted regression in ~4 minutes.

- 2026-08-24: AUTHORING A STAGED HEADFUL DRIVER, ROUND 2 — four more traps measured at `2026-08-23-headful-leg-extension`, none product-caused; they extend the 2026-08-23 three-trap entry. **(1) Label injection ≠ navigation.** The Tauri window label is init-script-injected into `about:blank` documents too, so a readable label can NEVER serve as a navigation signal — the leg's own handle dump showed `label=findings url=about:blank` in one line. The only navigation signal is `getUrl()` leaving `about:blank`. **(2) Assert a toggle by FLIP, never by scripted directions.** A hide-then-show script encodes assumed state; the assembled path leaves surfaces in states the script author did not model (the dashboard self-mounts HIDDEN and may never be shown), so every fixed-direction poll asserts the wrong direction and reads as four dead presses. The toggle CONTRACT is open-if-hidden/hide-if-shown — so read the state, press once, poll for its INVERSION, and record `{pressed, before, after, flipped}` per press. **(3) Gate DOM probes on measured visibility.** A hidden webview still renders content — the report window renders a first-active-incident FALLBACK while hidden, so an ungated `modal-dialog` probe was vacuously green on a window that never opened; likewise a click focuses its own button, so a focus-restore probe must be gated on the dismissal actually having happened. Visibility comes from the window API (`plugin:window|is_visible` by label — the same transport the app itself uses cross-window), never from DOM presence. **(4) RED-arm polarity.** `--expect-absent <STAGE>` asserts the stage is NOT observed, so as a STANDING gate it must pair with `--no-inject` naming a telemetry-dependent stage — `--expect-absent` alone against a healthy app exits FAILURE by design (measured as a plan Test-Commands defect at P5-validated planning; the P5 validation checks producer-presence, not arm polarity).

- 2026-08-25: A READ-ONLY OBSERVER STAGE MUST NOT PERTURB WHAT FOLLOWS IT — round 3 of the staged-headful-driver traps (2026-08-23 ×3, 2026-08-24 ×4). A stage that only READS still mutates shared state if it navigates, resizes, focuses, or dismisses to make its own assertion cheap, and the cost lands on LATER stages that never mentioned it. Measured: a `native-menu-suppressed` observer placed late in the leg clicked back to `/traces` so a canvas would be present for its P-065 half; that left downstream window state unlike the pristine flow and killed the RED arm's WebDriver session at `dashboard-close` (`ERROR webdriver: Couldn't resolve command with id …`), with the leg then never completing. **Fix by PLACEMENT, not by compensation** — re-home the observer to a point where the state it needs already holds (here, right after `traces-scroll`, where the leg is already on `/traces`), rather than navigating and trying to restore. Restoring is not equivalent: the pristine 13-stage RED arm ran 184s PASS, the same arm with the route change never completed across three ceilings (420 / 660 / 1200s), and the re-homed 15-stage arm ran 183s PASS. Corollary for diagnosis: **an ever-growing timeout is a symptom-fix** — three ceiling raises bought nothing because the leg was not slow, it was hung; when a raised ceiling does not change the outcome, stop raising and go find the hang.

- 2026-08-27: A `browser.execute` BODY IS SERIALISED TO THE WEBVIEW AND CLOSES OVER NOTHING — selectors, constants and helpers from the driver's module scope are NOT in scope inside it, so a selector used only there must be an inline literal (hoisting it to a `const` beside the other selectors leaves the constant dead and fails `no-unused-vars`). Prefer `browser.execute` over WebdriverIO element queries when the property under test is on a VISUALLY-HIDDEN node: a clip-rect live region returns empty from `getText()`, which applies visibility semantics, while a `textContent` read through the DOM returns the announced string. Both measured while authoring the `report-copy` stage at `2026-08-27-report-window-copy-affordance`.

- 2026-08-28: A HARNESS LEG THAT REPRODUCES A KNOWN OPEN DEFECT IS A **SCENARIO**, NOT A GATE — register it as one, and never green it. When a new leg turns a previously-irreproducible failure into an on-demand reproduction, its red is a TRUE POSITIVE about the product, not a regression of the chunk that built it and not external decay. The reflex to make a red command green is exactly wrong here: weakening the assertion, deleting the arm, or hiding it behind `--expect-absent` destroys the only reproduction anyone has. Register it explicitly OUTSIDE the standard gate set with three things attached — which arm (if any) IS gate-grade today, a named OWNER for turning the red arm green (a route entry, never "later"), and a never-weaken instruction — so the next reader meets a documented state rather than a mysteriously failing command. **This does NOT relax the `#[ignore]`-is-not-a-fix ban in testing.md** — that ban forbids HIDING a failure; this is its opposite, a failure kept maximally loud and given an owner. The discriminator is visibility: a scenario's red is recorded in the spec, the rules, and the handoff; a hidden failure is recorded nowhere. Corollary for the leg itself: make it prove its own preconditions, so a pass cannot be vacuous — the gap arm reports INCONCLUSIVE (not PASS) when the condition it exists to create never formed, and the control arm reports INCONCLUSIVE when that condition formed anyway, which is what stops two arms from being one test run twice. Verified at `2026-08-28-ingest-consumer-initiating-freeze` (`cargo xtask smoke:gap-resume`). **[extended 2026-08-28-ingest-consumer-block-under-gap-resume]** A third arm joined — `--reconnect-only`, which seeds then reconnects with NO idle gap — and it needed its OWN precondition rather than a share of arm A's: stormless by construction, it keys on FEED evidence (≥1 `duckdb.append`, `StormEvidence::fed()`) instead. **The general rule: when you add an arm to a self-proving leg, give it a precondition of its own; an arm that borrows a sibling's precondition either cannot pass or passes vacuously.**

- 2026-08-28: A LEG'S RUN WINDOW MUST OUTLAST THE THRESHOLD ITS VERDICT READS, or the verdict is structurally incapable of failing. A detector keyed on "N consecutive ticks" / "M seconds without progress" can only fire once the run has lasted that long, so shortening the observe window below it converts the leg into a guaranteed PASS — not a weaker signal, an absent one. The failure is invisible from the outside: the leg runs, the log is clean, the verdict says PASS, and nothing distinguishes it from a real pass. Measured this session: `cargo xtask smoke:gap-resume --observe-minutes=3` reported PASS while the consumer had in fact stopped, because the stall announcement needs 450 s (30 ticks) and a 3-minute window cannot reach it; the tell was the append count (232, against 233 in the run that failed), not the verdict. **Two habits: (a) before shortening any window "just to iterate faster", check what threshold the verdict reads and keep the window above it — or run the leg purely as a diagnostic and read its ARTIFACTS, never its verdict; (b) a leg whose verdict depends on a threshold should assert its own window against that threshold and refuse to report PASS when it cannot reach it.** This is the window-shaped member of the vacuity family in `rules/testing.md` (empty collection · stub payload · zero counter · redacted-observable predicate · defect-shape mismatch) — same failure, different mechanism: here the check is well-formed and the RUN is too short to exercise it.

- 2026-08-29: A HARNESS'S NEGATIVE FINDING ABOUT THE PRODUCT NEEDS A SECOND SOURCE BEFORE IT IS REPORTED AS A PRODUCT FACT — and its own absence message must not assert a cause it cannot distinguish. A leg that reads one field of one response and finds nothing has established that IT saw nothing, not that the thing does not exist; but the natural phrasing of such a verdict ("the storm did not form") is a claim about the SUT, and it reads as a measurement. Measured at `2026-08-29-app-registry-reconciliation`: `smoke:external-resolve` reported "the sidecar listed no active incident — the storm did not form" across two runs while the corpus held **2 rows with `status=active`** and the app log carried **3 `incident.created`**; the cause was a one-word accessor typo — `query_incident_list` returns `items[].incident_id`, and the leg read `items[].id`, so `.get("id")` yielded `None` on a perfectly healthy response. Three leg runs (~15 min) were spent on it, and the first two "findings" were about the harness, not the product. **Two habits.** (a) Before reporting an absence the leg observed, corroborate against a differently-sourced view — the obs log, a direct read of the store's plaintext columns, or the tool invoked BY HAND so its real response shape is visible; calling the sidecar manually is what exposed this in one step. (b) Word the INCONCLUSIVE branch to state only what was observed and enumerate the causes it cannot separate ("no active incident listed within Ns — no storm formed, or none survived the auto-resolve window"), never a single confident cause. This is the harness-side sibling of the 2026-08-15 emit-site-is-the-authority rule in `rules/observability.md`: that one governs what a target's silence may be read to mean; this governs what a HARNESS's silence may be read to mean.

- 2026-08-30: GIT-INDEX READS FOR STAGED-ARTIFACT GATES — the technique set measured at `2026-08-30-staged-bindings-assertion`, xtask's first git subprocess. (a) `git show :<repo-relative-path>` (forward slashes, literal) yields the INDEX blob — locally the about-to-be-committed copy, on a fresh CI checkout identical to HEAD, so ONE staged read serves both local commit-gating and CI commit-validation. (b) Order the probes: `git -C <root> ls-files --stage` FIRST as the repo-health probe (spawn/exec failure ⇒ cannot-evaluate, its own exit arm — never a findings pass), THEN per-subject `git show` with index-membership deciding the staged-DELETION arm (findings-red) — collapsing the two makes a broken git indistinguishable from a deleted subject. (c) Fixture repos for such gates need only `git init` + write + `git add` — NO commit, hence no `user.name`/`user.email` config, so TempDir fixtures run clean on any host and never touch the real tree. (d) Pin the discrimination PAIR: index-correct/worktree-clobbered must stay green (a worktree check false-REDs there) AND index-clobbered/worktree-repaired must red (the commit-risk shape a worktree check misses) — the pair, not either half, is what proves the gate reads the right subject.

- 2026-08-30: REVOKE-CYCLE MECHANICS, MEASURED END-TO-END at `2026-08-30-acl-rejection-logging` — two techniques for the by-hand capability-revoke arm. (a) **Leg-artifact preservation:** `cargo xtask webview-drive` prints `webview-drive: data_dir <path>` then DELETES that TempDir at process exit, so any post-run wire assertion against the app's own log must be captured DURING the run — a background watcher that polls the leg's output for the data_dir line, then re-copies `<dir>/logs/.` to a scratch dir every ~2s until the dir vanishes, preserves the full record (the last copy before deletion carried the revoked-run's 6,033 lines; the stage under test fires mid-leg, so dozens of snapshots follow it). Convert the printed Windows path via `cygpath -u` before `cp`. (b) **Staged-gates interplay holds by design, now measured:** a WORKTREE-only grant revoke never touches the index, so `check:staged-artifacts` and the folded capability-drift staged assertion stay green through the entire revoke → rebuild → drive → restore cycle, and `git checkout -- pulse-app/capabilities/<file>.json` restores byte-identical by construction (zero diff vs HEAD) — the restore-discipline half of the 2026-08-23 entry above is mechanically checkable, not remembered. Remember the re-embed rule: each side of the cycle needs its own `cargo build -p pulse-app --release` (the ACL is compile-embedded), and the leg's printed binary line is the freshness check.

- 2026-08-30: TWO cross-process path facts measured at `2026-08-30-agent-harness-teardown-truth`, opposite directions. (a) **MSYS/Git Bash CONVERTS exported path-shaped env values when spawning a native child** — `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR=/tmp/probe-x` reached a native process as `C:/Users/turbo/AppData/Local/Temp/probe-x` (live probe) — so "the shell and the app resolve the same env path to different filesystems" is NOT a real divergence mechanism on this host; measure with a one-line native-child `os.environ` probe before building a fix on that hypothesis. (b) **A default state path embedding `$$` diverges across INVOCATIONS, not processes**: each separate `agent-run.sh` verb ran under a fresh `$$`, so boot/status/cleanup as separate invocations minted three different `agent-run-$$` dirs and could never share a pidfile — cross-verb state needs one exported `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` (ci.yml provides it workflow-level at line 12; bare local runs get the loud `cleanup: no-pid-ports-accepting` exit 1 instead of the old silent success). Generalizes: never key cross-invocation harness state on `$$`.

- 2026-09-29: A CHILD CARGO SPAWNED BY A `cargo run`-LAUNCHED TOOL INHERITS THAT TOOL'S PACKAGE VARIABLES — `cargo run -p xtask` sets `CARGO_PKG_*` / `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` (and siblings) on xtask, and every `cargo` xtask spawns carries them. A build script that declares `rerun-if-env-changed` on them (ring does, for `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` and `CARGO_PKG_NAME` / `_VERSION_*`) then sees xtask's values in an xtask-launched build and none in a shell-launched one, so each alternation reruns it and recompiles everything above it (rustls, `libduckdb-sys`'s C++ build, every workspace crate) — on a full-match cache, in step after step. Every cargo child xtask spawns goes through `cargo_command()`, which drops them; a new spawn site uses it too. Two tells: the same crates `Compiling` in consecutive steps on a warm cache, and a long SILENT stretch at the start of a `cargo xtask` step — the alias is `run --quiet`, so xtask's own rebuild prints nothing. Probe: the crate's `target/*/build/{crate}-*/output` `rerun-if-env-changed` lines plus `CARGO_LOG=cargo::core::compiler::fingerprint=info` (`dependency on X is newer than we are`).

- 2026-10-04: An `npm ci` exit 0 that prints `npm warn install-scripts … held back` is NOT proof the install scripts did not run — on the Linux dev host puppeteer's browser download still started and was left PARTIAL, and a later env-isolated `npm ci` (the pre-push `npm` stage) then failed on that cache. Before re-running a red `npm` stage, run it with `PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR` set to a fresh absolute path under `target/`; never delete the shared `~/.cache/puppeteer/`. [corrected 2026-10-04: removing the partial folder buys ONE green `npm ci` — a fresh cache reproduces the partial v148 folders (the zip intact, extraction stopping after its first entries) while v152 installs whole, and a re-run against that cache fails again; founder ruling: isolate, never delete. Why extraction stops is unmeasured.]

- 2026-10-10: A runner-only failure that follows the version of a system LIBRARY is reproduced on the dev host by swapping that library in for one command: fetch the runner image's own package by URL, refuse it on a checksum mismatch, unpack it under `target/`, and name the unpacked directory through `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` on the leg's command alone. Local-first, zero-infrastructure modular monolith: every byte of telemetry stays on the developer's machine; fourteen library crates (seventeen workspace members total: those fourteen + the `pulse-app` binary crate + the `xtask` task-runner crate + the dev-only test-support library crate `test-support`, which no product target links — the canonical list is arch §Occupied Resources §Cargo workspace crate names, which any count word defers to) are wired by ONE shared engine boot, `pulse_app::engine_boot` (`init_process`, then `start`), which both entry points call — the Tauri window app (`pulse-app`) and the console program (`andromeda-pulse-engine`, `run` | `version` | `door`, no window; `door` boots no engine and relays a stdio agent's lines to a running engine's door); neither entry point wires an engine part itself (pinned by `pulse-app/tests/unit_engine_boot_seam.rs`). Within a program the crates share memory via tokio mpsc + broadcast (ingest → buffer → viz / MCP / snapshot subscribers), so the OS sees one engine process per program (since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door the console program's `door` word also runs as short-lived relay processes that host no engine part; PROVISIONAL with the door) and ingest→viz latency is microseconds. Standards-track at the edges (OTLP at `:4317`/`:4318`, MCP over stdio, WASM Component Model plugins) and tightly opinionated in the middle (TauRPC bridge, Arrow zero-copy hand-off, `serde`-friendly `AppError`) — external tooling Just Works while agent-driven development stays unambiguous. Capability-scoped extensibility: WASM plugins receive only the host imports declared in their WIT; Tauri's `pulse:default` capability is the negative-default trust model (no auth required because there are no user accounts).

_This section is curated by `/wrap-session`. It accumulates universal (Tier 1) rules captured from work sessions — rules that apply to every file and every task. Do not edit manually during wrap-session runs — changes are preserved but wrap-session appends new entries here._
- The product IS the local observer — `tracing` ecosystem only for self-observation; an OTel network exporter pointed at own `:4317`/`:4318` is infinite recursion.

- Tauri capabilities are negative-default at the core-API layer: a new TauRPC procedure needs router registration AND its `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` pin in `xtask/src/main.rs` — never a per-procedure `pulse-app/capabilities/` entry, which does not exist here — while a missing `fs` / `shell` / `dialog` / `http` / `core:window:*` grant IS silently rejected at runtime. [corrected 2026-10-06: the six capability files hold core and plugin permissions only, no procedure name]

- Telemetry is user-controlled content — incidentally captured secrets in OTLP attribute values mean snapshot files / clipboard / MCP tool responses / DuckDB query parameters NEVER appear verbatim in self-observation logs.
